areas.text: The grounds and the prison on them.

locations.name: East and West Lakes
locations.district: The Lakes and the Serpent's Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-21 · Danger: High]

The two great lakes south-west of Ba Sing Se, divided by the Serpent's Pass, the western joined by rivers to the Mo Ce Sea and the eastern to the Eastern Sea. Ferries cross the eastern lake to the city. A traveller sees the far shore as a line and the city's wall as another.

areas.name: Open Water
areas.text: The lake between the shores.

locations.name: Eastern Air Temple
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-15 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

One of the four Air Temples, on three mountain peaks joined by bridges off the south-eastern coast, once the home of the female airbenders and the most spiritual of the temples. Its people died in the genocide and its halls are empty but for Guru Pathik. A traveller climbs a long way.

areas.name: Bison Stables
areas.text: The empty stables of the temple's sky bison.

areas.name: Guru's Peak
areas.text: The peak where Pathik sits with his onion and banana juice.

areas.name: The Bridges
areas.text: The bridges between the peaks over a long drop.

locations.name: Ember Island
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The Fire Nation's resort island in the outer islands to the north: black-sand beaches, palm trees, luxurious vacation homes for the wealthy and the powerful, kuai ball on the sand and the Ember Island Players at the theater. High officials keep houses here, and the Fire Nation Royal Family keeps a beach house its children have not visited in years. A traveller sees first the ferry pier, the parasols and the ease of people who have never been near the war they are winning.

areas.name: Ferry Pier
areas.text:
The pier where the ferries and the Fire Navy's passenger sloops tie up, with the yard clerk's booth at its landward end and porters waiting for the rich.

The roads, ferries and cutters serves this yard: ferries sail to Fire Nation Capital (about 14 Pieces), River village (about 30 Pieces); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: The Beach
areas.text: The black-sand beach below the resort houses: kuai ball nets, parasols, the bonfires of the young and rich at night.

areas.name: The Royal Beach House
areas.text: The Fire Nation Royal Family's house on the shore, shuttered for years, its garden gone wild and its portraits of a family that no longer exists.

areas.name: Theater Steps
areas.text: The steps and foyer of the theater where the Ember Island Players perform, famous and terrible, with the island's whole society in the seats.

locations.name: Ember Island Theater
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-24 · Danger: High]

The playhouse on Ember Island where the Ember Island Players perform, famous across the Fire Nation for being very bad at it. The island's whole society fills the seats; the actors fill the stage with whatever the Fire Nation would like to be true. A traveller buys a ticket and learns what the enemy thinks of them.

areas.name: The Seats
areas.text: The tiers where the rich sit low and the poor sit high and everyone laughs at the same lines.

areas.name: The Stage
areas.text: The painted stage and its trapdoors, the actors in their paper armour.

locations.name: Fancy Lady Day Spa
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A spa in the Upper Ring built to pamper the upper-class women of the city, with mud, steam and attendants who have seen everything. A traveller with coin is made beautiful; without it, shown the door.

areas.name: Mud Baths
areas.text: The steam and the mud.

locations.name: Farming village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A small settlement in the western Earth Kingdom that avoided occupation through the war, a farming village with fields, a market and a small hospital. A traveller is treated kindly and asked for news.

areas.name: Farm Square
areas.text: The square and the market.

areas.name: Fields
areas.text: The farms around the village.

locations.name: Farming village hospital
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The small medical clinic of the farming village, a few cots, a doctor and herbs drying from the beams. A traveller with a wound is taken in without papers.

areas.name: The Ward
areas.text: The cots and the doctor's table.

locations.name: Fire Fountain City
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-20 · Danger: High]

A large industrial city on the second island of the Fire Nation, named for the great statue of Fire Lord Ozai at its centre with flame pouring from its hands. Factories, barracks, a crowded market, and a people who shout the Fire Lord's name with real feeling. A traveller sees the statue from the harbour and everything else after.

areas.name: Factory Row
areas.text: The iron works and the workers' streets.

areas.name: Fountain Harbour
areas.text: The city's harbour, where ferries and the navy's transports dock.

areas.name: Statue Square
areas.text: The square under the Fire Lord's statue, fire pouring from its hands.

locations.name: Fire Island Prison
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-24 · Danger: High]

A remote prison island in the northern Fire Islands, built to hold waterbenders by being entirely dry: no water within reach, nothing to bend. Hama was held in a place like this for years. A traveller sees bare rock and iron and understands the design.

areas.name: Dry Cells
areas.text: The cells, the dry air, the water brought in a cup under guard.

locations.name: Fire Nation Army factory
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-24 · Danger: High]

The army's smelting plant on the shore of the Jang Hui River, where metals for weapons and vehicles are made and a tough new armour steel is cooled with river water. Its smokestacks foul the air and its waste fouls the river that feeds Jang Hui. A traveller smells it before seeing it.

areas.name: Smelting Floor
areas.text: The furnaces and the vats, soldiers in masks and the heat.

locations.name: Fire Nation bazaar
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A large open-air market in the eastern Fire Nation selling top-quality Fire Nation goods: top-knot rings, headgear, eye patches, jewellery, food, and clothes that let a stranger pass for a local. A traveller can buy a disguise here, and a disguise is the first thing a traveller needs.

areas.name: Clothiers' Row
areas.text: The stalls of robes, armour trim and headgear.

areas.name: Food Stalls
areas.text: Fire flakes, flaming fire flakes and the rest.

locations.name: Fire Nation Capital
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The seat of the Fire Nation, built inside the crater of a dead volcano on Capital Island. The harbour lies below the crater's lip behind the Great Gates of Azulon; the Royal Plaza and the avenues climb to the Fire Nation Royal Palace at the crater's heart, with the Capital City Prison and the High Temple on the slopes. Fire Lord Ozai rules from here from 95 AG. A traveller sees first the steps from the harbour, the soldiers on them, and the banners: this city has never been attacked and does not expect to be.

areas.name: Harbour Steps
areas.text:
The long stair from the crater harbour up to the city, where every arrival is counted by the Domestic Forces. Coaches and ferries are booked at the clerk's table at the top of the steps.

The roads, ferries and cutters serves this yard: ferries sail to Ember Island (about 14 Pieces); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Palace Gate
areas.text: The outer gate of the Fire Nation Royal Palace, Royal Procession guards at either side and the Fire Sages' High Temple above. Nobody passes without a summons or a title.

areas.name: Plaza Approach
areas.text: The avenue up from the great square where the Fire Lord's proclamations are read and the army parades. Statues of past Fire Lords ring it; the people stand where they are told.

areas.name: Prison Road
areas.text: The road down to the Capital City Prison, where war prisoners and the Fire Lord's enemies are held. Carts go down full and come back empty.

locations.name: Fire Nation colonial village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A small Fire Nation colonial village in the north-western Earth Kingdom, a cultural centre of the colonies famous for its Fire Days Festival of fireworks, masks and firebending shows. A traveller with a mask can walk its festival; without one they are watched.

areas.name: Festival Street
areas.text: The lantern street where the Fire Days Festival is held.

areas.name: Garrison
areas.text: The soldiers' post at the town's edge.

locations.name: Fire Nation Royal Palace
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

The home of the Fire Nation Royal Family and the seat of its government, at the centre of the crater city, guarded day and night. Behind its gates are the throne room where Fire Lord Ozai sits behind a wall of flame, the royal apartments, the war room where the generals plan the comet, and the gardens where Zuko and Azula were children. A traveller sees it only from the gate unless summoned, and a summons is rarely good news.

areas.name: Fire Throne
areas.text: The long hall to the Fire Lord's throne, the flames before it rising with his temper and the courtiers kneeling at a distance measured in fear.

areas.name: Royal Gardens
areas.text: The pond and the turtle ducks, where a mother once taught her son to be kind.

areas.name: War Room
areas.text: The map room where the generals plan the war and the Fire Lord decides what to burn next.

locations.name: Fire Nation school
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A centre of learning in the eastern Fire Nation where the children recite the oath, learn the official history of the war and are forbidden to dance. The headmaster watches the yard. A traveller in uniform is assumed to be a student and treated like one.

areas.name: Classroom
areas.text: Rows of desks under the Fire Lord's portrait.

areas.name: Schoolyard
areas.text: The drill yard where the oath is sworn each morning.

locations.name: Firelight Fountain
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A romantic attraction in the Middle Ring, a fountain where citizens feed the turtle ducks by day and watch the lanterns lit around it by night. A traveller comes here with someone or wishes they had.

areas.name: The Fountain
areas.text: The fountain and its lanterns.

locations.name: Flower shop
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-24 · Danger: High]

A store near the Misty Palms Oasis owned by Fung, given over to flower arranging, with a back room where old men play a board game and speak in riddles. A traveller buys flowers or, with the right opening move, something else.

areas.name: Flower Counter
areas.text: Flowers in the front and the game in the back.

locations.name: Fog Marsh
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-40 · Danger: Deadly]

A marsh of the Spirit World where the fog is thick enough to lose a name in, and the voices in it are those who did. A traveller who stops to listen stays.

areas.name: Fog Water
areas.text: The fog and the voices.

locations.name: Foggy Swamp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-24 · Danger: High]

A vast, mysterious wetland in the south-western Earth Kingdom, dense with catgators, vines and fog, all of it one living thing under a banyan tree the size of a hill. A traveller sees visions here and is not sure which are the swamp's.

areas.name: Black Water
areas.text: The channels where the catgators wait.

areas.name: The Banyan
areas.text: The great tree at the swamp's heart.

locations.name: Foggy Swamp Tribe
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The village of the Foggy Swamp Tribe, one of the three Water Tribes, descended from southerners who settled the swamp long ago and bend the water in vines and fog their own way. A traveller is fed possum chicken and told the swamp is one tree.

areas.name: Stilt Village
areas.text: The huts on stilts and the fire.

locations.name: Full Moon Bay
locations.district: The Lakes and the Serpent's Pass
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 9-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A secluded cove on the eastern of the two lakes, south of Ba Sing Se, where the hidden ferry station takes refugees across the lake to the city. Every refugee from the south comes here with a passport and the fare or without them, and the ticket clerks of the Earth Kingdom ferry decide who crosses. A traveller sees first the cliff hiding the cove, then the crowd: families, deserters, merchants, a man with cabbages, all waiting.

areas.name: Ferry Station
areas.text:
The station hall where tickets are stamped and refused, the yard clerk at the counter and the ferries at the dock beyond.

The roads, ferries and cutters serves this yard: coaches run to Misty Palms Oasis (about 8 Pieces); ferries sail to Lower Ring (about 10 Pieces); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Refugee Camp
areas.text: The tents and fires of those still waiting for papers or money, where everything is for sale and nothing is safe.

areas.name: The Dock
areas.text: The lake dock where the ferries to Ba Sing Se load, guards checking passports a second time.

locations.name: Gaipan
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A small village in the western Earth Kingdom under Fire Nation occupation, in a river valley below a dam, where the soldiers take what they want and the villagers keep their heads down. The Freedom Fighters watch it from the trees. A traveller sees the red banners over a green village.

areas.name: Dam Street
areas.text: The one street, the garrison house at its head.

areas.name: The Dam
areas.text: The dam above the valley, and the water behind it.

locations.name: Gan Jin Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The camp of the Gan Jin tribe on the Great Divide's rim, refugees bound for Ba Sing Se, tidy, clean and proud of it, and feuding with the Zhang over a hundred-year-old wrong. A traveller is offered clean water and a lecture.

areas.name: Tidy Camp
areas.text: The tents in rows.

locations.name: Gaoling
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A large, old town in the mountains of the southern Earth Kingdom, rich at the top and poor at the bottom, with the Beifong Estate above it and Earth Rumble, the earthbending tournament, in its arena. Master Yu's academy teaches the rich; Xin Fu runs the tournament for everyone else. The war has not come here and the town acts as if it never will. A traveller sees first the gate, the caravan yard, and the posters for Earth Rumble.

areas.name: Beifong Estate
areas.text: The walled estate of the richest family in the town, gardens, guards and a daughter nobody outside has seen.

areas.name: Caravan Yard
areas.text:
The yard by the town gate where the coaches and caravans load, the yard clerk's table under an awning and ostrich horses in the pens.

The roads, ferries and cutters serves this yard: coaches run to Omashu (about 8 Pieces), Misty Palms Oasis (about 9 Pieces); ferries sail to Wolf Cove (about 24 Pieces); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Earth Rumble Arena
areas.text: The rock arena where Earth Rumble is fought, the Boulder and the rest throwing rocks for a crowd that pays for it.

areas.name: Master Yu's Academy
areas.text: The earthbending academy where the town's sons learn forms they will never use.

locations.name: Garsai
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A city in the western Earth Kingdom, the site of a battle early in the war that Azulon won for his father and that the Fire Sages still recall at funerals. It has been a colony for generations. A traveller sees the monument before the market.

areas.name: Old Quarter
areas.text: The Earth Kingdom streets behind the colonial ones.

areas.name: Victory Square
areas.text: The square with the monument to Azulon's battle.

locations.name: General Fong's fortress
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A secluded Earth Kingdom military base in the mountains of the west coast, one of the last strongholds of the Earth Kingdom in the region, with barracks, an infirmary, a temple and guest quarters. Its position faces the Fire Nation across the sea. A traveller is received by a general who wants something.

areas.name: Infirmary
areas.text: The large infirmary for the war's wounded.

areas.name: Parade Court
areas.text: The courtyard where the general receives guests and drills troops.

locations.name: Great Divide
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-21 · Danger: High]

The largest canyon in the world, in the rocky centre of the Earth Kingdom, a link between the refugee towns and Ba Sing Se for those who dare it: no food may be carried in, and the canyon crawlers come for whoever carries it. A canyon guide takes parties across. A traveller crosses in a day or not at all.

areas.name: Canyon Floor
areas.text: The floor and the crawlers' holes.

areas.name: Canyon Rim
areas.text: The rim where the guide gathers the parties.

locations.name: Great Gates of Azulon
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-30 · Danger: Severe]

The sea gate of the Fire Nation Capital, built early in Fire Lord Azulon's reign: a great net held between statues of Azulon and two dragons, raised across the strait and set alight when a ship comes that should not. A traveller passes under it on any ship that enters the harbour, and the crew goes quiet.

areas.name: The Strait
areas.text: The water between the statues, the net sunk below the surface and the watch posts on either cliff.

locations.name: Hama's village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A small town on one of the central islands, where people have been disappearing on full-moon nights for years and the townsfolk blame a moon monster. The innkeeper is a kind old woman from somewhere far south. A traveller is warned not to go out under the full moon.

areas.name: Moonlit Street
areas.text: The town's one street, shuttered early on the nights of the full moon.

areas.name: The Inn
areas.text: Hama's inn, warm, clean and welcoming, with a cellar nobody is shown.

locations.name: Han Tui
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-21 · Danger: High]

A city of the northern Earth Kingdom captured early in the war when Fire Lord Sozin burned its drought-dry defences to the ground in minutes. It has been a Fire Nation colony since, rebuilt in red over the black stones of the old city. A traveller sees the burn marks under the new paint.

areas.name: Burned Quarter
areas.text: The old streets never rebuilt.

areas.name: Colonial Square
areas.text: The square with the governor's house.

locations.name: Harbor town
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A small coastal settlement in the south-western Earth Kingdom that stayed free of Fire Nation control through the war, a fishing and trading town with a market and a harbour. A traveller sees green banners and relaxes.

areas.name: Fishing Harbour
areas.text: The fishing harbour and its boats.

areas.name: Free Market
areas.text: The town's market, open to all nations.

locations.name: Harbour Quarter
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

The town on the harbour below the crater's lip, where the capital's ships unload and its sailors drink: warehouses, chandlers, taverns, the Fire Navy's berths and the coal yards that feed them. It is the one part of the capital a foreigner can move through without papers, as long as they are buying. A traveller sees the hulls first and the crater above them second.

areas.name: Sailors' Row
areas.text: The taverns and lodging houses between the docks and the stair.

areas.name: The Docks
areas.text: Berths, cranes and the coal yards, sailors and dockers everywhere.

locations.name: Healers' Hut
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-24 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The healing hut of Agna Qel'a where the tribe's eldest healer teaches its women the healing water and the chi paths, the art the North allows them. A traveller hurt in the North is brought here.

areas.name: Healing Pool
areas.text: The healing pool and the lesson.

locations.name: Hei Bai's Grove
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 15-30 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The grove on the spirit side where Hei Bai, the forest spirit of the scorched forest, rests when he is not a monster, a bamboo stand of great calm. A traveller who comes with an acorn is welcome.

areas.name: Bamboo Grove
areas.text: The bamboo and the spirit.

locations.name: High Temple
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe]

The Fire Sages' sanctuary in the Fire Nation Capital, directly north of the Fire Nation Royal Palace, where the Fire Lords are crowned and buried. An Avatar born in the Fire Nation comes here when told what he is, as Avatar Roku did. Under its floor lie the Dragonbone Catacombs. A traveller sees the pillars and the sages, and is not shown the stair.

areas.name: Sanctuary
areas.text: The sages' hall of offering, the eternal flame and the records of the royal line.

locations.name: Iceberg Field
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-9 · Danger: Low]

The sea ice north of Wolf Cove where the tribe fishes from canoes among the bergs and where, in the winter of 99 AG, a girl's temper cracked a berg and let out a boy and a bison. A traveller fishes here and watches the ice.

areas.name: The Bergs
areas.text: The ice and the canoe lanes between.

locations.name: Inner Wall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-30 · Danger: Severe]

The inner wall of Ba Sing Se, around the three rings of the city proper, with gates where papers are read and the monorail passes through. A traveller passes it with a passport and a Joo Dee waiting on the other side.

areas.name: Inner Gate
areas.text: The gate between the farms and the city.

locations.name: Iroh and Zuko's apartment
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-24 · Danger: High]

An upper-class residence in the Upper Ring, the home of two refugees from the Lower Ring after the tea-maker's fortune changed. A traveller calling here finds an uncle at home and a nephew out.

areas.name: The Rooms
areas.text: The apartment's rooms.

locations.name: Jang Hui
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A small fishing village of houseboats and stilt houses in the middle of the Jang Hui River, joined by bridges and planks, on one of the outer islands. The river feeds it and the Fire Nation Army factory upstream poisons it. A traveller sees the planks, the thin people and the colour of the water.

areas.name: The Planks
areas.text: The walkways between the houseboats, fishing nets drying and nobody fishing.

areas.name: Village Dock
areas.text: The dock where the day's thin catch is sold.

locations.name: Jang Hui River
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The river on an island of the eastern Fire Nation that gives Jang Hui its name and its fish and clams, with the village in its middle and the army's factory on its shore poisoning it. A traveller follows it from the sea to the smoke.

areas.name: The Reach
areas.text: The river between the village and the factory.

locations.name: Jasmine Dragon
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-24 · Danger: High]

A traditional tea shop in the Upper Ring, a failing business until an old refugee tea-maker took it over and made it the best in the city, named for drama, poetry and a nice ring. A traveller drinks the best tea in Ba Sing Se and is asked how their day was.

areas.name: Tea Room
areas.text: The tea room and its counter.

locations.name: Ketu Harbor
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-24 · Danger: High]

A Fire Nation military port in the south-western Earth Kingdom, occupied for decades, where the navy docks and resupplies for its assaults on the Earth Kingdom and keeps watch on the Southern Water Tribe. A traveller sees the iron first and the fort behind it.

areas.name: Naval Yard
areas.text: The docks and the fort.

locations.name: Kolau Mountain Range
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-24 · Danger: High]

The great chain of mountains of the south-western Earth Kingdom, the birthplace of earthbending, holding Omashu on one peak and the Cave of Two Lovers under another. The passes are high and, from the spring of 100 AG, held by the Fire Nation. A traveller crosses by the pass, the tunnel, or not at all.

areas.name: Badgermole Country
areas.text: The slopes above the tunnels.

areas.name: High Pass
areas.text: The mountain road over the range.

locations.name: Kolau Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: High]

The Fire Nation's checkpoint on the mountain road through the Kolau Mountain Range, held from the spring of 100 AG with tanks and a barricade, where every traveller's papers are read twice. A traveller without papers turns back toward the tunnel.

areas.name: Barricade
areas.text: The barricade, the tanks and the table where papers are read.

locations.name: Kuanming Square restaurant
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

An eatery on Kuanming Square in the Middle Ring, a hidden jewel of the lower and middle classes, reasonably priced and never likely to reach the upper ring's tables. A traveller eats well and overhears much.

areas.name: The Tables
areas.text: The bistro's tables and its cook.

locations.name: Kyoshi Island
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

An island off the southern coast of the Earth Kingdom, once a peninsula until Avatar Kyoshi split it from the land, dotted with small villages and famous for its elephant koi and the warriors who keep its name. Some of its villages have never let a stranger stay. A traveller sees the statue of Kyoshi from the sea.

areas.name: Koi Bay
areas.text: The bay of the elephant koi and the thing that eats them.

areas.name: Kyoshi's Statue
areas.text: The great painted statue of Kyoshi on the shore.

locations.name: Kyoshi Landing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The island's fishing port below Kyoshi's statue, where the elephant koi are landed and the mainland traders buy them. A traveller lands here and is met.

areas.name: The Quay
areas.text: The koi quay and the traders' boats.

locations.name: Kyoshi Shrine
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 3-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A sanctuary on Kyoshi Island dedicated to Avatar Kyoshi after her death, once a village temple, keeping her headdress, fans, kimono and boots. The path to it is sacred. A traveller is shown the relics by the village elder, if the elder approves.

areas.name: Relic Hall
areas.text: The hall of Kyoshi's relics.

locations.name: Lake Laogai
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe]

A large lake in the Agrarian Zone, a pleasant place for a day out according to the Joo Dees, with a high-security prison under it where Long Feng interns anyone whose actions cross his plans and the Dai Li do their brainwashing. A traveller swims here or is taken here.

areas.name: Lake Shore
areas.text: The lake and its shore.

areas.name: Under the Lake
areas.text: The prison's tunnels and the chamber with the lamp.

locations.name: Lakeshore Camp
locations.district: The Lakes and the Serpent's Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The camp on the eastern lake's shore where refugees who cannot or will not take the ferry wait for a boat, a guide or courage. A traveller finds families, deserters and a man selling cabbages.

areas.name: Shore Camp
areas.text: The tents and the fire.

locations.name: Lee Family Pig Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-9 · Danger: Low]

A small farm on the southern plains run by Gansu and Sela, with an old farmhouse, a pig pen, a thatched barn and a field of sunflowers, sold in the nearby town. A traveller is fed and asked to help with the roof.

areas.name: Farmhouse
areas.text: The weathered house and the pig pen.

locations.name: Lower Ring
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The outermost residential ring of Ba Sing Se, home to the city's poor and most of its people: industries, food, cloth, medicine, slums, and the refugees the ferry brings every day. The Dai Li police it from the shadows and the law ignores it otherwise. The Pao Family Tea House is here, and so, in the spring of 100 AG, are two Fire Nation refugees under false names. A traveller sees first the monorail terminus, the wall above everything, and the Joo Dee smile of the woman assigned to them.

areas.name: Monorail Terminus
areas.text:
The station where the monorail from the Outer Wall ends and the ferries' passengers arrive, the yard clerk's window for passage out, and a Joo Dee waiting for each new face.

The roads, ferries and cutters serves this yard: coaches run to Northern Air Temple (about 12 Pieces); ferries sail to Full Moon Bay (about 10 Pieces); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Pao Family Tea House
areas.text: A small tea house in a poor street, where an old man serves the best tea in the ring and his nephew sulks.

areas.name: The Slums
areas.text: The crowded alleys where refugees sleep and crime lives, and where the Dai Li's rock gloves come at night.

areas.name: Workshop Street
areas.text: The ring's trades: smiths, dyers, potters, the smell of work and the sound of the monorail overhead.

locations.name: Mai's house
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe]

One of the elegant homes of the Fire Nation nobility, directly across from the Royal Palace, where Mai's family lives when her father is not governing somewhere. Quiet rooms, dark lacquer, servants who know when not to speak. A traveller comes here on a noble's errand or not at all.

areas.name: Reception Hall
areas.text: The hall where callers wait under the family's banners and are rarely welcome.

locations.name: Makapu Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A small farming village on the slopes of Mt. Makapu in the north-western Earth Kingdom, where the fortune teller Aunt Wu reads the clouds and the whole village lives by what she says. A traveller is read a fortune whether they ask or not.

areas.name: Aunt Wu's House
areas.text: The fortune teller's house, with its bone fire and its queue.

areas.name: Cloud Square
areas.text: The square under the mountain where the clouds are watched.

locations.name: Master Yu's Earthbending Academy
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The earthbending school in Gaoling run by Master Yu, where the town's sons learn forms for a fee and the master flatters their fathers. A traveller can watch a lesson from the gate and learn what Gaoling thinks earthbending is.

areas.name: Training Court
areas.text: The court where the forms are drilled and the stances praised.

locations.name: Middle Ring
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-30 · Danger: Severe]

The middle ring of Ba Sing Se, the home of its merchants, scholars and craftsmen: Kuanming Square, the university, the Firelight Fountain and the shops that serve the upper ring. A traveller with money walks here freely; without it, briefly.

areas.name: Kuanming Square
areas.text: The square and its restaurants.

areas.name: Shop Street
areas.text: The shops of the ring.

locations.name: Mining village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A minor settlement near the Mo Ce Sea shoreline in the western Earth Kingdom, a coal-mining village under Fire Nation occupation where earthbending is forbidden and the benders have been taken to the prison rig. A traveller sees the pit heads and the fear.

areas.name: Miners' Houses
areas.text: Houses under the Fire Nation's post.

areas.name: Pit Head
areas.text: The mine entrance and the coal carts.

locations.name: Misty Palms Oasis
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 9-27 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A town on the south-western edge of the Si Wong Desert, grown from a seedy cantina around a spring of ice that is melting. Traders, soldiers, sandbenders and wanderers crowd it, because it is the last place to rest and buy before the desert and the first place to drink after it. A traveller sees first the gate, the palms, and the cantina's doorway where everyone who crosses the Si Wong is sooner or later seen.

areas.name: Caravan Gate
areas.text:
The gate where the caravans and sand-sailers assemble, the yard clerk's booth beside it and the fares to the four roads chalked up.

The roads, ferries and cutters serves this yard: coaches run to Omashu (about 10 Pieces), Gaoling (about 9 Pieces), Full Moon Bay (about 8 Pieces), Northern Air Temple (about 12 Pieces); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: The Cantina
areas.text: The oasis cantina: mango drinks, sandbenders at the back, a professor with maps, and every rumour of the desert for the price of a drink.

areas.name: The Spring
areas.text: The oasis's ice spring under the palms, shrinking every year, where the town's water is drawn and its quarrels begin.

locations.name: Mountain Hermitage
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 9-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small shrine on a ledge of the Taihua Mountains on the road to the Northern Air Temple, kept by a hermit who remembers when the monks came down this way, with prayer flags and a kettle. A traveller is given tea and silence.

areas.name: Ledge Shrine
areas.text: The ledge, the flags, the kettle.

locations.name: Mt. Makapu
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A large volcano above Makapu Village. Its last eruption, in the winter of 99 AG, was turned from the village by a trench the villagers dug and the Avatar's bending. A traveller climbs it for the view and the heat.

areas.name: The Crater
areas.text: The rim and the lava below it.

locations.name: Nan Shan River
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A small river in the southern Earth Kingdom that empties into the South Sea, strong in places and calm in others, with pools ideal for bathing or for washing a sky bison. A traveller rests here and is found here.

areas.name: River Pools
areas.text: The calm pools and the rapids above them.

locations.name: Noble Hill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-30 · Danger: Severe]

The slope of the crater where the Fire Nation's noble houses stand, mansions behind lacquered gates above the common streets, Mai's house among them. Sedan chairs, servants, a quiet that is really watchfulness. A traveller with a noble's invitation is admitted; without one, questioned.

areas.name: Tea Pavilion
areas.text: A pavilion where the nobles' wives take tea and the news.

areas.name: The Gates
areas.text: The lane of great houses, each gate with its crest and its porter.

locations.name: North Pole Tundra
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-27 · Danger: Severe]

The North Pole continent beyond the city, tundra, polar desert and mountain, surrounded by the Northern Sea and held by the tribe's hunters. A traveller goes out with a hunter or does not come back.

areas.name: Open Tundra
areas.text: The open tundra.

locations.name: Northern Air Temple
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 9-24 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

One of the four Air Temples, on a peak of the Taihua Mountains along the continent's north coast, emptied in the Air Nomad Genocide and settled a generation ago by Earth Kingdom refugees under the mechanist after a flood took their village. His machines and his son Teo's gliders have filled the temple with steam, pipes and noise. A traveller sees first the gliders in the wind, then the smoke where no smoke should be.

areas.name: Glider Hall
areas.text: The hall where Teo and the children fly their gliders from, the wind roaring through the open side of the mountain.

areas.name: Mountain Road Station
areas.text:
The station at the foot of the climb where the mountain coaches turn and the yard clerk sells passage; above it the lift to the temple.

The roads, ferries and cutters serves this yard: coaches run to River village (about 12 Pieces), Misty Palms Oasis (about 12 Pieces), Lower Ring (about 12 Pieces); ferries sail to Agna Qel'a (about 36 Pieces); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: The Old Sanctuary
areas.text: The airbenders' sanctuary, its statues and murals half hidden behind steam pipes.

areas.name: The Workshop
areas.text: The mechanist's workshop, inventions and half-inventions everywhere, and a locked door nobody discusses.

locations.name: Northern Coast Watchtower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-21 · Danger: High]

A Fire Navy watchtower on the cliffs of the Northern Sea, watching the water for the North's boats and the mountains for the temple's gliders, with a signal fire the fleet reads. A traveller is seen before they see it.

areas.name: Signal Tower
areas.text: The tower and its fire.

locations.name: Northern Fishing Grounds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

The sea ice and open water off Agna Qel'a where the tribe's boats fish and hunt seal, under the wall's watch. A traveller goes out with a crew and learns what cold is.

areas.name: The Leads
areas.text: The open water between the ice.

locations.name: Northern Water Tribe Royal Palace
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-30 · Danger: Severe]

The seat of the Northern Water Tribe's government in Agna Qel'a, the chief's house, seen from almost anywhere in the city, where Chief Arnook and his advisers sit and decide for the tribe. A traveller is received at a feast or not at all.

areas.name: Chief's Hall
areas.text: The hall where the chief and his advisers sit.

locations.name: Old Southern Harbour
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-9 · Danger: Low]

The ruin of the Southern Water Tribe's old harbour city, left when the raids took the benders who built it, broken walls of stone and ice that the village lives beside and does not use. A traveller sees what the South was before the war.

areas.name: Harbour Ruin
areas.text: The broken harbour and the old chief's seat.

locations.name: Omashu
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The second city of the Earth Kingdom, built up a peak of the Kolau Mountain Range in stepped terraces, with the delivery system's chutes running down it on earthbending and gravity. An army of earthbenders guards the gate, and King Bumi, old, mad and the strongest earthbender alive, rules it. Omashu holds free until the spring of 100 AG, when it surrenders and becomes New Ozai. A traveller sees first the bridge to the gate, the guards' rock, and the packages flying overhead.

areas.name: Gate Yard
areas.text:
The yard inside the great gate where the coaches and ostrich-horse carts wait and the yard clerk books passage. Earthbender guards check every cart's cabbages.

The roads, ferries and cutters serves this yard: coaches run to River village (about 10 Pieces), Gaoling (about 8 Pieces), Misty Palms Oasis (about 10 Pieces); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Lower Terraces
areas.text: The markets and houses of the lower city, the mountain wind in every street and the chutes' rumble overhead.

areas.name: Peak Palace
areas.text: King Bumi's palace at the peak, with its throne room, its feasts and its three challenges for anyone he finds interesting.

areas.name: The Chutes
areas.text: The delivery system's stone chutes running down the terraces, packages and the occasional fool sliding through the city on earthbending and gravity.

locations.name: Omashu Royal Palace
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-24 · Danger: High]

The palace of the monarch of Omashu at the top of the city's peak, its every door worked by earthbending so that no one but an earthbender can enter or leave. It holds a waterfall hall, King Bumi's pet goat gorilla Flopsie and an arena for his challenges. A traveller enters at the king's pleasure.

areas.name: Challenge Arena
areas.text: The arena where the king's tests are given.

areas.name: Throne Hall
areas.text: Bumi's throne, his feasts and his three challenges.

locations.name: Outer Wall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-30 · Danger: Severe]

The outer wall of Ba Sing Se, the greatest wall in the world, raised and held by earthbenders, with the Agrarian Zone's farms behind it and the plain before it. The Terra Team holds its top. It has never been breached. A traveller arriving by land sees it for a day before reaching it.

areas.name: The Battlements
areas.text: The top of the wall, the Terra Team's ground.

areas.name: Wall Gate
areas.text: The gate where the monorail passes through the wall.

locations.name: Ozai's beach house
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-24 · Danger: High]

The Fire Nation Royal Family's vacation home on Ember Island, once the most beautiful estate on the island, shuttered and rundown since the family stopped coming. Portraits of a family that no longer exists hang in its halls; the garden has gone wild. A traveller who gets past the gate finds a house that remembers.

areas.name: The Courtyard
areas.text: The overgrown courtyard where a prince once burned a portrait.

areas.name: The Hall
areas.text: The shuttered hall with its dusty portraits and a family tree carved over the hearth.

locations.name: Pass Northern Gate
locations.district: The Lakes and the Serpent's Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-21 · Danger: High]

The northern end of the Serpent's Pass where the rock meets the land under the Outer Wall of Ba Sing Se, an Earth Kingdom guard post checking whoever comes off the pass. A traveller arrives wet and is questioned.

areas.name: Guard Post
areas.text: The post at the pass's end.

locations.name: Pass Southern Gate
locations.district: The Lakes and the Serpent's Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-21 · Danger: High]

The southern end of the Serpent's Pass, two posts and a carved warning to abandon hope, where those without a passport decide whether to walk. A traveller reads the carving and looks at the water.

areas.name: The Posts
areas.text: The posts and the carving.

locations.name: Patola Mountain Range
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The mountains on the Southern Archipelago in the South Sea, north of the South Pole, the Air Nomads' territory with the Southern Air Temple at their centre. The peaks are reached by air or by a very long climb. A traveller sees the temple's spires from the sea and no way up.

areas.name: The Peaks
areas.text: The high range and its cloud.

locations.name: Penguin Slopes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low]

The snow slopes near the village where the otter penguins gather and the children sled on them, with a fish for bait. A traveller who has never laughed in the South laughs here.

areas.name: Sled Slopes
areas.text: The slopes and the penguins.

locations.name: Piandao's castle
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-24 · Danger: High]

The lavish estate of the sword master Piandao high on the cliff over Shu Jing: sixteen bedrooms, two gardens, a foundry where swords are made, stables, and a white lotus on the front gate and the courtyard floor. He takes the student he chooses and sends the rest away. A traveller is received by the butler and judged.

areas.name: Foundry
areas.text: The forge where the master's swords are made.

areas.name: Lotus Courtyard
areas.text: The lotus courtyard where the master tests a student with a brush, a stone and a sword.

locations.name: Plains village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A small, poor town on the arid plains of the southern Earth Kingdom, held by a few Earth Kingdom soldiers who have become its bullies. A traveller sees the dust, the poverty and the soldiers' swagger.

areas.name: Plains Market
areas.text: What the plains farmers can sell.

areas.name: The Street
areas.text: The town's one street and its soldiers.

locations.name: Pohuai Stronghold
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A Fire Nation fortress in the western Earth Kingdom near the ruins of Taku, three walls deep, commanded by Shinu, its colonel, and home to the Yuyan Archers, who can pin a fly to a tree at a hundred paces. A traveller does not come here willingly.

areas.name: The Keep
areas.text: The inner keep where prisoners of value are chained.

areas.name: The Walls
areas.text: The three rings of wall, the gates and the towers with the archers on them.

locations.name: Prison rig
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The Fire Nation's offshore prison in the Mo Ce Sea, an iron rig miles from land where earthbenders taken for resisting are held with no earth to bend and made to build and refuel the navy's ships. The warden is unforgiving. A traveller arrives in a hold.

areas.name: Coal Hold
areas.text: The hold where the rig's coal is kept.

areas.name: The Deck
areas.text: The iron deck and the cells below it.

locations.name: Quarry campsite
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A campsite in a quarry in the south-eastern Earth Kingdom, cut rock and flat ground, where travellers stop between the coast and the desert. A traveller finds shelter from the wind and nothing to eat.

areas.name: The Quarry
areas.text: The quarry floor and the fire ring.

locations.name: Realm of Koh
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-40 · Danger: Deadly]

A realm of the Spirit World that is home to the ancient spirit Koh, the face stealer, a cave under a dead tree where every face he has taken lives on his body. He takes the face of anyone who shows feeling before him. A traveller enters with no expression or does not leave with one.

areas.name: Koh's Cave
areas.text: The cave and the thing in it.

locations.name: River village
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 3-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A medium-sized Earth Kingdom town between the forks of a large river on the Mo Ce coast, a regional trading hub where merchants sell whatever the river brings. Pirates trade openly from their ship at the quay, scrolls and curiosities among the rest, and nobody asks where the cargo came from. A traveller sees first the bridges, the stalls and the mixed crowd of farmers, river boatmen and men with too many knives.

areas.name: Forks Landing
areas.text:
The landing where the river boats, the coast ferries and the coaches meet, the yard clerk's shed at its head and the fares chalked on a board.

The roads, ferries and cutters serves this yard: coaches run to Omashu (about 10 Pieces), Northern Air Temple (about 12 Pieces); ferries sail to Ember Island (about 30 Pieces), Agna Qel'a (about 40 Pieces); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Market Bridges
areas.text: The stalls on the bridges between the forks: food, cloth, charms, maps, and the pirates' shop with its curiosities and its guard.

areas.name: Pirate Quay
areas.text: The quay where the pirates' ship ties up, a reptile bird on its rail and the captain's men watching the town watch them.

locations.name: Roadside kiosk
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-9 · Danger: Low]

A small government newsstand on a road in the north-western Earth Kingdom, one of thousands planted across the country to post the state's news and notices. Wanted posters go up here first. A traveller reads it and learns who is being hunted.

areas.name: The Board
areas.text: The notice board and its posters.

locations.name: Roku's island
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A small isle that was Avatar Roku's home in his later years, with a cottage where he lived with Ta Min and a cave in the cliff behind it where his dragon lived, until the eruption that killed him. A village once stood here too. A traveller finds ash, ruin and a very old silence.

areas.name: The Ruin
areas.text: What the eruption left of Roku's cottage and the village below it.

locations.name: Royal Palace gardens
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe]

The gardens in the courtyard of the Fire Nation Royal Palace, where the royal family takes its leisure and once gave garden parties for the nobility. Zuko and Azula spent their childhood here with their mother, feeding the turtle ducks. A traveller sees them from the colonnade and no closer.

areas.name: Turtle Duck Pond
areas.text: The pond, the turtle ducks and the bench.

locations.name: Royal Plaza
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe]

The long forum in the harbour just below the Fire Nation Capital, where the royal family holds rallies and the army parades, and the capital's main line of defence: battlements, catapults and a gate between cliffs that an invader cannot go around without miles of detour. A traveller lands here and is counted here.

areas.name: Battlements
areas.text: The walls and engines facing the sea, manned at every hour.

areas.name: Forum
areas.text: The parade ground and its stands, the Fire Lord's dais at the crater end.

locations.name: Royal spa
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe]

The Fire Nation Royal Family's private health resort in the capital, one of Princess Azula's favourite places, where she has her hair washed and her nails done while the attendants tremble. A traveller enters as a servant or not at all.

areas.name: The Chair
areas.text: The spa and the princess's chair.

locations.name: Sandbender Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

A camp of the Si Wong tribes in a dune hollow, tents and sand-sailers, a chief and his sons, the rules of the desert and no others. A traveller is given water, which is the whole of the law, and then watched.

areas.name: The Hollow
areas.text: The tents and the sailers.

locations.name: Scorched forest
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Moderate]

Hilly woodland with a small river near Senlin Village, burned in 99 AG by a Fire Nation battle, its guardian spirit enraged by the loss. Acorns still fall in the ash. A traveller walks through it quickly.

areas.name: The Burn
areas.text: The black heart of the forest.

locations.name: Sea Wall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-30 · Danger: Severe]

The great wall of ice that faces the Northern Sea before Agna Qel'a, raised and held by waterbenders, with the sea gate in its middle. It has turned every attack for a hundred years. A traveller sees it from the sea as the end of the world.

areas.name: Wall Top
areas.text: The top of the wall and the benders on it.

locations.name: Seaport village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A small coastal settlement on the Mo Ce Sea, an important port captured by the Fire Nation, where coal from inland is loaded into warships before they go out to sea. The prison rig stands miles offshore. A traveller sees the warships first and the village only around them.

areas.name: Coaling Quay
areas.text: The quay where the warships take on coal.

areas.name: Fishers' Lane
areas.text: What is left of the village's own life.

locations.name: Secluded hot springs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

Hot springs on a remote Fire Nation island, surrounded by volcanic rock, walls and waterfalls, with nobody for miles. A traveller who finds them can rest in peace, for a while.

areas.name: Hot Pools
areas.text: The hot pools under the falls.

locations.name: Seedy merchants pier
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A trading port in the south-western Earth Kingdom where merchants from every corner of the world meet to make whatever money they can: jewellery, pottery, tsungi horns, bison whistles, and con artists in every other stall. All nations are welcome who can pay. A traveller keeps a hand on their purse.

areas.name: Pier Stalls
areas.text: The pier's stalls, junk and treasure side by side.

areas.name: Pirates' Berth
areas.text: Where the pirates' ship ties up when it is in.

locations.name: Senlin Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A small farming village at the edge of the scorched forest, unoccupied because the Fire Nation saw nothing worth taking, where the villagers farm, trade and keep a shrine to the forest's spirit. A traveller is welcomed and warned about the nights.

areas.name: Hei Bai's Shrine
areas.text: The small shrine at the forest's edge.

areas.name: Village Green
areas.text: The green and the headman's house.

locations.name: Serpent's Pass
locations.district: The Lakes and the Serpent's Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

A narrow strip of rock between the East and West Lakes, one of the few direct paths to Ba Sing Se, named for the serpent that guards it and feared across the nation. Most refugees take the ferry instead. A traveller walks it with the water on both sides and the serpent beneath.

areas.name: The Gap
areas.text: The place where the path goes under the water.

areas.name: The Spine
areas.text: The narrow path on the rock.

locations.name: Shipwreck
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-9 · Danger: Low]

A massive Fire Nation naval vessel tilted and uprooted in the ice near the Southern Water Tribe, left from the first of the Southern Water Tribe raids, the ship the tribe's waterbenders stopped. The children are told not to go in. A traveller goes in.

areas.name: Tilted Hull
areas.text: The tilted decks and the room with the trap.

locations.name: Shu Jing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A small, peaceful town on a cliff of waterfalls on one of the eastern islands, one of the many settlements tucked away in the Fire Islands and far from the war. Piandao's castle stands above it. A traveller sees the waterfalls first, then the quiet, then the castle.

areas.name: Cliff Road
areas.text: The road up through the town past the falls.

areas.name: Market Square
areas.text: The small square where the town sells what it grows.

locations.name: Si Wong Desert
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-27 · Danger: Severe]

The largest, driest and hottest desert in the world, at the heart of the Earth Kingdom, almost impossible to cross, home to the Si Wong tribes and the beetle-headed merchants and to nobody's law. A traveller who enters without a guide is a story the oasis tells later.

areas.name: Cactus Flats
areas.text: The flats where the cactus grows and its juice is not to be drunk.

areas.name: The Dunes
areas.text: The open sand.

locations.name: South Pole Ice
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The South Pole continent, the southernmost land in the world, frozen tundra, polar desert and dangerous mountains, with the Southern Water Tribe on its northern shore and nothing else for days. A traveller who goes inland needs a reason and a sled.

areas.name: Polar Ice
areas.text: The open ice.

locations.name: Southern Air Temple
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 3-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

One of the four Air Temples, in the remote Patola Mountain Range, the home of the male airbenders until the Air Nomad Genocide, thought reachable only by sky bison. Its courtyards are empty, its air ball court silent, and in its sanctuary the statues of every Avatar wait. A traveller who gets here is almost certainly flying.

areas.name: Avatar Sanctuary
areas.text: The hall of the statues of every Avatar, opened by airbending.

areas.name: Gyatso's Chamber
areas.text: The side chamber with the bones and the armour.

areas.name: Temple Courtyard
areas.text: The courtyard and the air ball court.

locations.name: Spirit Library
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-40 · Danger: Deadly]

Wan Shi Tong's Library on the Spirit World's side, where it stands whole after its keeper pulled it out of the desert in 100 AG, the knowledge of the world on its shelves and the owl who no longer trusts humans at its door. A traveller who comes as a spirit may read; one who comes with a question of war is refused.

areas.name: Spirit Stacks
areas.text: The stacks on the spirit side.

locations.name: Spirit Oasis
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 15-40 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A lush garden and pond in a cove deep within Agna Qel'a, made by Tui and La, the moon and the ocean, and warm when everything around it is frozen. Tui and La, the two koi, circle each other in the pond, white and black; the air is heavy and the water is the most powerful healing water in the world. It is the most peaceful place in the North and the nearest door to the Spirit World. A traveller sees first the green, then the warmth, then the fish.

areas.name: The Far Side
areas.text: What a meditating mind finds past the pond: fog, a path, trees that are not trees, and the Spirit World beginning.

areas.name: The Gate
areas.text: The wooden gate in the ice wall between the oasis and the city, the Northern Water Tribe's guards outside it.

areas.name: The Pond
areas.text: The pool where Tui and La circle, the bridge over it and the grass that stays green in the ice. Sitting here is the crossing.

locations.name: Spirit Roads
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-35 · Danger: Deadly]

The paths that join the Spirit World's realms, roads of light and dark that spirits travel and a crossing mind can follow if it keeps its purpose. A traveller who loses the thread of why they came loses the road.

areas.name: Light Road
areas.text: A road of light between realms.

locations.name: Spirit Woods
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-35 · Danger: Deadly]

The woods a crossing mind first walks into on the Spirit World's side: trees that watch, fog that moves against the wind, paths that are not where they were. Spirits pass here on their own errands. A traveller who shows fear is noticed.

areas.name: The Clearing
areas.text: A clearing where spirits gather.

areas.name: The Fog Path
areas.text: The path through the fog.

locations.name: Suki's village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A small farming village on Kyoshi Island, the most isolationist on the island and the home of Suki and the Kyoshi Warriors, who drill in the dojo and guard the shore. A traveller is tied to a post until they prove they are not Fire Nation.

areas.name: Dojo
areas.text: The warriors' hall, fans on the wall.

areas.name: Warriors' Street
areas.text: The wooden houses and the post where strangers are tied.

locations.name: Taihua High Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-21 · Danger: High]

The one road over the Taihua Mountains between the Mo Ce coast and the temple, with a Fire Nation post at its summit and tanks that cannot leave it. A traveller pays the toll in papers or in a long detour.

areas.name: Summit Post
areas.text: The post at the top of the road.

locations.name: Taihua Mountains
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-24 · Danger: High]

The great chain of mountains across the northern Earth Kingdom, from south of Ba Sing Se west to the Northern Air Temple, high, cold and crossed by few roads. The Fire Nation holds the western passes and the Earth Kingdom the eastern. A traveller crosses in days and sleeps cold.

areas.name: Taihua Passes
areas.text: The high roads over the range.

areas.name: The Valleys
areas.text: The hidden valleys between the ridges.

locations.name: Taku
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A largely abandoned city on the shore of the north-western Earth Kingdom, its walls fallen and its streets empty since the war's early years. An old herbalist keeps her institute in the ruins with her cat. A traveller comes for a cure or for shelter and finds both, grudgingly.

areas.name: Herbalist's Institute
areas.text: The old woman's tower of herbs, jars and her cat.

areas.name: The Ruins
areas.text: The fallen city around it.

locations.name: Tavern
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A tavern in a dangerous part of a west-coast town near a trading port, welcoming people from any nation as long as they do not say which, where money is gambled away and there is a fight every night. A traveller comes here to find someone who is not supposed to be found.

areas.name: Taproom
areas.text: The low room, the dice, the fight.

locations.name: Team Avatar's Upper Ring house
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-24 · Danger: High]

A one-storey house of three bedrooms in the Upper Ring, part of a lady's manor, given to the Avatar's party with furnishings, services and a Joo Dee free of charge. A traveller invited here is watched from the street.

areas.name: The House
areas.text: The rooms and the courtyard.

locations.name: Tu Zin
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A small abandoned mining village in a deserted valley of the southern Earth Kingdom, some distance from the desert, with nothing in it but dust and old works. A traveller finds shelter and nothing else.

areas.name: Empty Street
areas.text: The empty street between the empty houses.

locations.name: Upper Ring
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-30 · Danger: Severe]

The upper ring of Ba Sing Se, the home of its nobility, its generals and its guests of state, with the Earth Kingdom Royal Palace at its centre and the Jasmine Dragon on one of its streets. A traveller enters by invitation and is followed.

areas.name: Garden Street
areas.text: The nobles' gardens and the tea shop among them.

areas.name: Palace Approach
areas.text: The avenue to the palace.

locations.name: Village resort
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-15 · Danger: Moderate]

A lavish recreational centre on a river near the west coast, once a retreat for Earth Kingdom monks and now under Fire Nation control, where officers rest between campaigns. A traveller in uniform is welcome; in anything else, not.

areas.name: The Baths
areas.text: The river baths and their pavilions.

locations.name: Wan Shi Tong's Library
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-27 · Danger: Severe]

An enormous library devoted to all knowledge, kept by the spirit Wan Shi Tong and his fox knowledge-seekers, buried almost to its top in the central Si Wong Desert until 100 AG, when its keeper took it back to the Spirit World. A traveller who finds the one spire above the sand climbs down into the dark with a candle.

areas.name: Planetary Calendar Room
areas.text: The chamber where the sun and moon's dates are read.

areas.name: The Spire
areas.text: The one spire above the sand and the rope down.

areas.name: The Stacks
areas.text: Shelves without end and the foxes that run them.

locations.name: Waterfall lagoon
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A system of springs and waterfalls upriver from the ocean in the western Earth Kingdom, a hidden paradise for travellers with water enough to practise waterbending or simply to rest. A traveller finds it by going upriver past the point where the road gives up.

areas.name: The Falls
areas.text: The falls and the pool.

locations.name: Waterfall pond
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A waterfall pond on the northern outskirts of the Si Wong Desert, a respite for travellers who have crossed it and the last water before the Serpent's Pass. A traveller drinks first and looks second.

areas.name: The Pool
areas.text: The pool under the fall.

locations.name: West Lake Fishing Village
locations.district: The Lakes and the Serpent's Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A fishing village on the western lake's shore under the Serpent's Pass, where the catch goes to Ba Sing Se and the fishers watch the pass for the serpent and the Dai Li for the fishers. A traveller buys fish and passage on a boat that is not the ferry.

areas.name: Fishers' Houses
areas.text: The village and its headman.

areas.name: Fishers' Shore
areas.text: The boats and the nets.

locations.name: Western Air Temple
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-24 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

One of the four Air Temples, in the mountains north of the Fire Nation, built under the edge of a cliff with its spires pointing down so that nobody who did not know would see it. Its halls are empty since the genocide; the wind still flows through them. A traveller reaches it by climbing down.

areas.name: The Halls
areas.text: The hanging halls and the game boards nobody has played at for a century.

areas.name: The Spires
areas.text: The inverted spires and the rooms inside them.

areas.name: Upper Terrace
areas.text: The fountain terrace at the cliff's edge, the first place a visitor stands.

locations.name: Whaletail Island
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-9 · Danger: Low]

An island of the Southern Archipelago in the South Sea, off the south-western coast of the Earth Kingdom and north of the Southern Air Temple, shaped like a whale's tail. Water Tribe lore says no whale will come near it. A traveller lands here on the way south.

areas.name: The Tail
areas.text: The beaches of the island's two flukes.

locations.name: Wolf Cove
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The Southern Water Tribe's village on the shore of the South Pole continent: a handful of igloos and tents behind a low snow wall, with a watchtower that leans. The Southern Raiders took the last waterbender years ago, and Hakoda took the men to war in 97 AG; Kanna, Katara, Sokka, the children and the old are what is left. A traveller sees first how small it is, then how carefully it is kept.

areas.name: Landing Beach
areas.text:
The ice beach where the canoes and the cutters land and the yard clerk's job is done by whoever is oldest. The sea is the only road.

The roads, ferries and cutters serves this yard: ferries sail to Gaoling (about 24 Pieces); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Snow Wall Village
areas.text: The igloos and tents inside the snow wall, the fire pit, the elders' tent and the children playing at war.

areas.name: The Ice Fields
areas.text: The frozen sea beyond the village, where fishing is done and strange things surface.

locations.name: Yon Rha's village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A minor settlement in the hilly, rainy south of the Fire Nation, where a retired Southern Raiders commander lives with his mother and does the shopping. Nothing else happens here. A traveller sees a market, rain and an old man with a basket.

areas.name: Village Market
areas.text: The market in the rain where the old man buys vegetables.

areas.name: Yon Rha's House
areas.text: A small house on the hill with a demanding mother in it.

locations.name: Zhang Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The camp of the Zhang tribe on the Great Divide's rim, refugees bound for Ba Sing Se, rough, loud and proud of it, feuding with the Gan Jin over the same old wrong. A traveller is offered food and a story.

areas.name: Rough Camp
areas.text: The tents in a heap.

factions.name: Ba Sing Se University
factions.info: The greatest university in the world by its own account, in the grove district of the Middle Ring of Ba Sing Se, educating the Earth Kingdom's scholars and exchange students from the other nations, with faculties of anthropology, history and the rest and expeditions that go looking for the things the books describe. Zei, a professor of anthropology, has spent his career looking for Wan Shi Tong's Library. A stranger with a question finds a scholar; a stranger with a map finds a professor. One sworn to the university studies, copies, digs, and rises by what they bring back.

factions.name: Council of Five
factions.info: The five highest generals of the Earth Kingdom's army, the highest authority in its military, who oversee the whole war from a chamber in Ba Sing Se under General How, with General Sung among them holding the Outer Wall. The council also commands the Royal Earthbender Guards. It has not seen the Earth King in years. A stranger does not meet the council; an officer of rank waits a month to. One sworn to the council serves its chamber as a runner, a clerk, an aide, a staff officer, and rises by carrying what the generals cannot be seen to carry.

factions.name: Cultural Ambassadors
factions.info: The women assigned as guides to every important guest of Ba Sing Se in the late war, all called Joo Dee, all with the same calm, polished, mechanical smile, whose work is to keep outside influences from the city and the city's rule of silence from being broken. They are the first face a guest sees and the last. A stranger of rank is given one; a stranger without rank is reported by one. One sworn to the ambassadors is a smile at a guest's elbow, and rises by the Dai Li's satisfaction with how little the guest learned.

factions.name: Dai Li
factions.info: The elite secret police of Ba Sing Se, founded by Avatar Kyoshi to protect the city's cultural heritage, who capture, interrogate and imprison anyone who threatens the peace of the city as Long Feng, the city's grand secretariat, defines it. Men in green robes and conical hats with stone gloves on their hands, moving on the rooftops and in the earth. A stranger is watched from the ferry; a stranger who mentions the war is visited. One sworn to the Dai Li keeps the city's peace and the city's secrets, and rises by learning which is which.

factions.name: Domestic Forces
factions.info: The Fire Nation's law and home guard: the police of its cities and islands, the keepers of its prisons from the Capital City Prison to the Boiling Rock, the last line against an invasion and the trainers of the army's recruits. Its officers are mostly women, and they are the ones who read a stranger's papers, post the wanted notices and take a deserter away. A stranger is checked, filed and watched; a foreigner is checked twice. One sworn to the Domestic Forces keeps the Fire Lord's peace at home, guards what the war has taken, and rises by being the officer nobody gets past.

factions.name: Earth Rumble
factions.info: The underground earthbending tournament in a giant earthen arena in Gaoling, a popular show whose front rows are destroyed by flying rocks every night, hosted and promoted by Xin Fu, with the Boulder and his rivals on the bill and a champion nobody can beat. It is a business and a fight club and a family. A stranger buys a seat; a stranger with money gets a bout. One sworn to Earth Rumble fights in the ring under a name, takes the purse or the dirt, and rises by the crowd, which is the only judge.

factions.name: Ember Island Players
factions.info: The acting troupe of the Ember Island Theater, the island's only playhouse, who have no reputation for quality and take themselves entirely seriously, and who pack the house every night with the Fire Nation's best people. They stage the war as the Fire Nation would like it, and in the summer of 100 AG they put on a play about the Avatar that the Avatar himself sits through. A stranger buys a ticket; a foreigner buys one and keeps quiet. One sworn to the troupe carries a spear in the back row, learns the lines, and rises by being given a face the audience will remember.

factions.name: Fire Army
factions.info: The land arm of the military of the Fire Nation, the most powerful army in the world, a standing force loyal to the Fire Lord that overran most of the Earth Kingdom in a hundred years of war. Its regiments hold the colonies, its tanks and komodo rhinos lead its charges, its firebenders break walls and its conscripts fill the gaps. It drills on the crater floor of the capital and ships out from its harbour. A stranger is a recruit, a prisoner or a problem; a foreigner is a prisoner. One sworn to the Fire Army marches where it is sent, holds what it takes, and rises by holding it when the Earth Kingdom tries to take it back.

factions.name: Fire Nation air force
factions.info: The air arm of the military of the Fire Nation, the newest and smallest: the war balloons the mechanist's designs gave it, and in the last summer of the war the airships, built in secret for the comet. Its crews are picked firebenders and engineers who answer to the war minister and the Fire Lord. It was born at the Northern Air Temple, where the mechanist built the first war balloon, and flies from there and from the capital's drill ground. A stranger is kept away from the balloons; a foreigner is kept further. One sworn to the air force flies, keeps the burners and the secrets, and rises by being trusted with the ships the comet is for.

factions.name: Fire Nation circus
factions.info: A travelling circus of the Fire Nation and its colonies: rope walkers, acrobats, plate jugglers, a ring master and a collection of rare animals from a lion vulture to a platypus bear, entertaining Fire Nation and Earth Kingdom families alike wherever the tents go up. Ty Lee ran away to it. A stranger buys a ticket; a stranger who can walk a rope is hired. One sworn to the circus performs, feeds the animals and moves the tents, and rises by the act the crowd remembers.

factions.name: Fire Nation colonies
factions.info: The Fire Nation's continental empire: the Earth Kingdom and old Air Nomad territories it has taken over a hundred years, governed by Fire Nation governors over a mixed people of settlers and the conquered, from the Fire Nation colonial village and Garsai and Han Tui to the coaling ports of the Mo Ce coast. Trade between the colonies and the homeland feeds the war and the governors' purses. A stranger is a settler, a subject or a suspect, by accent; a foreigner is a subject. One sworn to the colonies serves a governor's house: a clerk, a garrison officer, a tax farmer, a magistrate, and rises by keeping a colony quiet and its tribute full.

factions.name: Fire Nation Royal Family
factions.info: The ruling family of the Fire Nation, which has held the throne for centuries through feuds, marriages and the struggle for absolute power. Fire Lord Ozai rules from the Fire Nation Royal Palace; Azula is his heir in all but name, Zuko his banished son, Iroh his brother who gave up a siege and a claim. The family is served by the Royal Procession, flattered by the nobles and feared by everyone else. A stranger meets it only as a petitioner, a prisoner or a spectacle at a rally, and a foreigner meets it as a prisoner. One sworn to the family serves its household: a page, a courier, a guard, a tutor, a spy, and rises by being useful and never, ever seen to want more.

factions.name: Fire Navy
factions.info: The sea arm of the military of the Fire Nation, the fleet that joins an archipelago into a nation and carries its war to every other shore: iron cruisers, catapults, the blockades that keep the Earth Kingdom's coast and the North's sea, and the armada that gathers for the comet. Its ships coal at the seaport village and the Fire Nation's home harbours, and its admirals answer to the Fire Lord alone. A stranger on a Fire Navy deck is cargo; a foreigner is a prisoner. One sworn to the Fire Navy sails where it is sent, keeps the blockade, and rises by taking what the sea gives: a prize, a port, an Avatar.

factions.name: Fire Sages
factions.info: The religious authority of the Fire Nation, the keepers of its temples from the High Temple in the capital to the Crescent Island Fire Temple, who crown and bury the Fire Lords, marry the royal family, and find the Avatar when he is born in the Fire Nation. They once served the Avatar; for a hundred years they have served the Fire Lord. A stranger is given a blessing and a lecture; a foreigner is given the lecture. One sworn to the Fire Sages tends a temple's flame, keeps its records, and rises by learning what the records say and when to keep silent.

factions.name: Five-Seven-Five Society
factions.info: A society of young women of Ba Sing Se's richest families who practise the art of traditional haiku under a strict madame, with poetry meetings, tea parties, garden parties and a guard who throws out anyone unworthy of the art. A line with a syllable too many is a disgrace. A stranger is admitted if invited and expelled on the first bad line; a stranger who counts well may stay. One sworn to the society composes, recites and judges, and rises by the madame's silence, which is praise.

factions.name: Foggy Swamp Tribe
factions.info: The third of the Water Tribes, descended from southerners who settled the Foggy Swamp long ago and bend the water in its vines and fog in a way neither pole would recognise, living in stilt huts in leaf skirts, eating possum chicken and believing the whole swamp is one tree. Huu guards it as a swamp monster. A stranger is fed and shown the banyan; a stranger who harms the swamp meets the monster. One sworn to the tribe learns the vines, the fog and the tree, and rises by understanding what the tree shows.

factions.name: Freedom Fighters
factions.info: A band of Earth Kingdom refugee teenagers and children under Jet, fighting the Fire Nation from a treetop hideout near Gaipan with hook swords, traps and ambushes, meaning to rid the world of firebenders whatever it costs the people in the way. They steal from the occupiers and feed the occupied, and they are children. A stranger is tested and recruited or tied up; a Fire Nation stranger is a target. One sworn to the Freedom Fighters lives in the trees, fights the way Jet fights, and rises by Jet's regard, which is quick to give and quick to take back.

factions.name: Gan Jin
factions.info: A tribe of the northern Earth Kingdom driven south by the war and bound for Ba Sing Se, proud, orderly and clean to the point of religion, who have feuded with the Zhang for a hundred years over a sacred orb and a thief. They camp at the rim of the Great Divide and will not cross with the Zhang. A stranger is offered washed water and a lecture on hygiene; a dirty stranger is offered the lecture. One sworn to the Gan Jin keeps the tribe's rules, which are many, and rises by keeping them where the Zhang can see.

factions.name: Kyoshi Warriors
