factions.info: An order of female warriors named for Avatar Kyoshi, who founded them to keep her island, one band to each village, fighting with war fans, face paint and footwork no army teaches and keeping Kyoshi Island apart from the war. In the winter of 99 AG a band under Suki leaves to help the defenceless on the mainland. A stranger on the island is tied to a post by them until proven harmless; a Fire Nation stranger stays tied. One sworn to the warriors learns the fans, the paint and the stance, and rises by the band's trust and a captain's nod.

factions.name: Military of the Earth Kingdom
factions.info: The armed forces of the Earth Kingdom, an army, a navy and the specialised divisions that have held the Fire Nation off for most of a hundred years: earthbender regiments in green, the garrisons of the free cities, General Fong's fortress on the west coast, the Outer Wall's defenders and the Council of Five over all of it. It has lost the west and the colonies and held the walls. A stranger is a recruit or a refugee to be sent on; a Fire Nation stranger is a prisoner. One sworn to the military marches in green, holds a wall or a fort, and rises by the council's notice, which comes slowly and to the living.

factions.name: Northern Water Tribe
factions.info: The chiefdom of the North Pole, the oldest of the Water Tribes, ruled by Chief Arnook from Agna Qel'a and kept for a hundred years by its sea wall, its waterbenders and its isolation. Master Pakku teaches the men to fight and the healers teach the women; its customs are old and hard. It has never fallen and never fought, until the Siege of the North. A stranger is a guest at the chief's feast and a curiosity in the canals; a Fire Nation stranger is a prisoner. One sworn to the tribe keeps the wall, the canals or the hunt, and rises by the chief's word and the master's.

factions.name: Omashu
factions.info: The monarchy and the earthbender army of Omashu, the Earth Kingdom's second city, under King Bumi, who guards its gate, runs its delivery system and supplied the Earth Kingdom's army with troops until the Fire Nation took the city in the spring of 100 AG. Its guards check every cart's cabbages; its king sets challenges for anyone interesting. A stranger is tested, housed and fed, in that order; a Fire Nation stranger is housed first. One sworn to Omashu serves its gate, its chutes or its court, and rises by the king's amusement, which is harder than it looks.

factions.name: Omashu Resistance
factions.info: The rebels who mean to free Omashu from the Fire Nation after its capture in the spring of 100 AG, earthbenders and ordinary citizens in the sewers and chutes, led by a few of the king's old guards, faking a plague to empty the city and keep its people out of the governor's hands. A stranger is a possible agent until proven otherwise; a Fire Nation stranger is a hostage. One sworn to the resistance moves through the tunnels, carries messages and food, and rises by what they are trusted to know.

factions.name: Pirates
factions.info: A pirate crew who scour the western seas for loot under a captain with an iguana parrot on his shoulder, selling their curiosities from their ship's deck when they dock at the river village and the seedy merchants pier: scrolls, charms, a monkey statue, and whatever the Fire Navy's cargo ships have lost. They would do almost anything for a reward. A stranger is a customer; a stranger with a purse is a mark; a stranger who steals is hunted. One sworn to the crew sails, steals, sells, and rises by what they bring aboard.

factions.name: Rough Rhinos
factions.info: An elite band of komodo rhino cavalry who ride for the Fire Lord on a freelance basis, paid by the job and loyal to the pay: a colonel, an archer, an explosives man, a chain fighter and a bender, each with his beast. They burn a town in an afternoon and are gone by night. They raid the southern coast and the plains and have ridden against Chin Village. A stranger is a target or a client; a foreigner is a target. One sworn to the Rough Rhinos rides, fights from the saddle, and rises by being the rider the colonel does not have to look back for.

factions.name: Royal Earthbender Guards
factions.info: The Earth King's personal protectors, earthbending warriors who belong to neither the army nor the Dai Li: they guard the Earth Kingdom Royal Palace, keep the gates of the Outer and Inner Walls, command the city's own troops and watch over everything the Earth King owns. They take their orders from the Council of Five. A stranger meets them at the gates with a passport in hand; a stranger without one meets them longer. One sworn to the guards keeps a gate or a palace door, and rises by never having let the wrong person through.

factions.name: Royal Procession
factions.info: The Fire Nation Royal Family's personal and ceremonial guard, an elite of firebenders in the skull masks and black armour that stand at every palace gate and ride with the Fire Lord's military moves. They guarded Azula's ship, they stand behind the throne, and they do not speak to anyone below a minister. A stranger sees them as a wall; a foreigner sees them as the last thing before the prison. One sworn to the Royal Procession guards the family with their body and their fire, and rises by being the one the family stands behind.

factions.name: Si Wong tribes
factions.info: The people of the Si Wong Desert, loosely organised tribes of nomads, guides, traders, raiders and scavengers who bend loose sand instead of solid earth and cross the dunes on sand-sailers, effectively independent of the Earth Kingdom that stops at the desert's edge. A stranger with water is a guest; a stranger with a sky bison is a sale. One sworn to the tribes rides the sailers, learns the sand, and rises by the desert's own law, which is water given and water owed.

factions.name: Southern Raiders
factions.info: A Fire Navy special unit raised to raid the Southern Water Tribe, capture or kill its waterbenders and end any hope of resistance in the south, which it did, raid by raid, until the South had none left; it struck the Earth Kingdom's coast between raids. Its ships bring black snow before them. Its commanders retire to quiet villages. A stranger is of no interest to it; a Water Tribe stranger is. One sworn to the Southern Raiders sails south under sealed orders, does what the orders say, and rises by not asking what they were for.

factions.name: Southern Water Tribe
factions.info: The federation of the South Pole's small tribes, ruled by a council of elders who elect its chief, once thriving with a waterbending style of its own and now stripped of its benders by the Southern Raiders and of its men by the war: Hakoda's warriors have fought the Fire Navy from Chameleon Bay and the Black Cliffs since 97 AG, and Kanna keeps the village at Wolf Cove. A stranger is fed and asked for news of the men; a Fire Nation stranger is a prisoner if the children can manage it. One sworn to the tribe fights with Hakoda or keeps the village, and rises by the warriors' trust, which is given on the water.

factions.name: Terra Team
factions.info: An elite platoon of earthbenders under General Sung charged with defending the Outer Wall of Ba Sing Se, organised and coordinated, in the army's uniform with their own colour of helm and armour. They have never let anything through. A stranger sees them on the wall's top as small green figures; a soldier sees them as the best. One sworn to the Terra Team holds the wall, raises the stone, and rises by the platoon's trust, which is earned on the battlements.

factions.name: Yuyan Archers
factions.info: An elite company of Fire Nation archers under the command of Shinu at the Pohuai Stronghold, who can pin a fly to a tree from a hundred paces without killing it, used for the stealthy missions where precision decides everything and counted among the Fire Nation's secret weapons. They took the Avatar alive in the winter of 99 AG. A stranger does not see them; an enemy sees one arrow. One sworn to the Yuyan Archers trains the eye and the stillness, goes where the colonel sends, and rises by the shot nobody else could make.

factions.name: Zhang
factions.info: An Earth Kingdom tribe that has feuded with the Gan Jin for centuries, driven from its lands by the war and bound for Ba Sing Se, rough, loud, generous and dirty, and proud of all four. They camp at the rim of the Great Divide and will not cross with the Gan Jin. A stranger is fed from the pot and told the feud; a tidy stranger is told it twice. One sworn to the Zhang eats, fights and laughs with the tribe, and rises by what they carry across the canyon.

creatures.name: Air Nomad
creatures.info: An airbender of the Air Nomads, in orange and yellow with arrow tattoos and a staff that opens into a glider, vegetarian, peaceful and quicker than anything alive. There is one in the world in the window. Fights by not being where the blow lands, and with gusts, scooters and the wind.

creatures.name: Ba Sing Se citizen
creatures.info: A citizen of Ba Sing Se, of whichever ring, in green with the city's calm, who has never heard of the war and will not thank you for mentioning it. Polite, prosperous or poor, careful. Fights only by calling the Dai Li, which is worse.

creatures.name: Baboon spirit
creatures.info: An anthropomorphic baboon spirit of the Spirit World, often found meditating near the Realm of Koh and irritated by anyone who interrupts. Fights with a shove and a hum of annoyance.

creatures.name: Badgerfrog
creatures.info: A furry hopping animal of the western Fire Nation, a croaker in the night at any temple or ruin. Harmless, loud, a comfort to the sleepless. Fights by hopping away.

creatures.name: Badgermole
creatures.info: An enormous blind digging mammal of the Earth Kingdom's mountains, the first earthbender and the teacher of the first humans who learned it, moving through rock as through water. Gentle unless provoked, fond of music. Fights with earthbending that reshapes the tunnel and claws that reshape the intruder.

creatures.name: Boar-q-pine
creatures.info: A large tusked boar covered in quills that inhabits most of the world's wild places, a carnivore that charges anything. Fights with tusks and a quilled flank nothing wants to touch.

creatures.name: Bounty hunter
creatures.info: A bounty hunter of the Earth Kingdom's coast, in leather and attitude, with a shirshu or a sword and a price list. Takes any nation's money and keeps her word to the letter. Fights with a whip, a blade and the shirshu's paralysing tongue, and leaves when the pay stops.

creatures.name: Buffalo yak
creatures.info: The Northern Water Tribe's great shaggy beast of burden, carrying supplies and sleds across the ice. Slow, strong and patient. Fights with horns and a shove.

creatures.name: Buzzard wasp
creatures.info: A large winged scavenger of the Si Wong Desert, a bird with a wasp's body, that comes in a swarm to the library's spire and the dying. Fights with a sting and a carry-off.

creatures.name: Canyon crawler
creatures.info: A many-legged, many-nostrilled hunter of the Great Divide that smells food from the rim and climbs the walls to reach it, in packs. Fast, relentless, tameable with a full stomach. Fights with jaws that kill quickly.

creatures.name: Cat owl
creatures.info: A hybrid of the forests of the Earth Kingdom and the Fire Nation, an owl with a cat's face and a meow-hoot nobody forgets, a hunter of mice and a pet of the odd. Fights with talons from a branch.

creatures.name: Catgator
creatures.info: A cat-whiskered alligator of the Foggy Swamp, fearsome to look at and a popular pet in the swamp and beyond. Lazy until hungry. Fights with a bite from the black water.

creatures.name: Circus performer
creatures.info: A performer of the Fire Nation circus: a rope walker, an acrobat, a juggler, an animal keeper, in pink and gold with chalk on the hands. Cheerful on the road, sharp-eyed about the ring master. Fights with tumbling, a thrown plate and a very fast exit.

creatures.name: Colonial settler
creatures.info: A Fire Nation settler of the colonies, born on the continent, in red over Earth Kingdom cloth, keeping a shop, a farm or a garrison post in a town that was someone else's. Wary of the homeland's officers and of the locals alike. Fights with whatever is to hand and a shout for the garrison.

creatures.name: Curly-tailed blue nose
creatures.info: A primate-like spirit of the Spirit World with a curled tail and a blue nose, curious, chattering and harmless, a guide if it likes you. Fights not at all.

creatures.name: Dai Li agent
creatures.info: An agent of the Dai Li in the green robe and conical hat with stone gloves on his hands, on a rooftop or in a wall, watching for anyone who mentions the war. Courteous, exact, unreadable. Fights with the rock gloves that grip and pin and with earthbending through the city's own stone.

creatures.name: Domestic Forces guard
creatures.info: An officer of the Domestic Forces, most often a woman, in the home guard's black and red with a baton, a whistle and a notebook, reading papers at a gate or walking a prison corridor. Polite, exact and impossible to hurry. Fights with a baton and a call for the watch, and firebends if she must.

creatures.name: Dragon
creatures.info: The original firebender, a long winged serpent that breathes fire in every colour, hunted to extinction for glory since Fire Lord Sozin made the kill an honour, the world says, the last one slain by General Iroh. Ancient, judging, beyond any human's strength. Fights with fire that is the whole sky, and does not need to.

creatures.name: Dragon hawk
creatures.info: The Fire Nation's messenger hawk, a raptor of the home jungles trained to carry a scroll across the sea and the continent. Proud, fast, loyal to the hand that feeds it. Fights with talons if cornered and is more often caught than killed.

creatures.name: Dragon moose
creatures.info: A horned draught animal of the Fire Islands' hot volcanic country, bred to pull the carriages of the nobility. Placid in harness, bad-tempered loose. Fights with horns and hooves when startled.

creatures.name: Earth Kingdom earthbender
creatures.info: An earthbender of the Earth Kingdom in green, army or militia or a village's own, rooted, patient, slow to move and impossible to move once set. Raises walls, throws stones, sinks tanks. Fights from the ground up and loses on a metal deck.

creatures.name: Earth Kingdom soldier
creatures.info: A soldier of the Earth Kingdom's army in green and the conical helm, a spear, a shield and a wall at his back, holding a fort or a gate for a king he has never seen. Stubborn, steady, tired of losing ground. Nonbender; fights in a shield line and calls for the earthbenders.

creatures.name: Earth Rumble fighter
creatures.info: A fighter of Earth Rumble under a ring name, in the costume that goes with it, throwing rocks at a crowd's roar. Loud, vain, better than he looks or worse. Fights with earthbending for show and for money, and is not used to losing to a girl.

creatures.name: Eel hound
creatures.info: A long four-legged creature that runs over land and swims as fast, the fastest ride in the world for a messenger or an invasion. Tireless and obedient. Fights with a bite and is better used to leave.

creatures.name: Elbow leech
creatures.info: A large parasitic worm of the Foggy Swamp's waters that fixes to the elbow with a small mouth and drinks. Slow, persistent, revolting. Fights by not letting go.

creatures.name: Elephant koi
creatures.info: A brightly coloured fish the size of a boat in the bay of Kyoshi Island, the island's export and the unagi's food, ridden by the foolish. Placid and strong. Fights with a slap of the tail and a dive.

creatures.name: Elephant mandrill
creatures.info: A trunked, coloured-faced primate of the Earth Kingdom's hills, large, loud and territorial. Fights with the trunk and a bite.

creatures.name: Ember Island player
creatures.info: An actor of the Ember Island Players in paper armour and a painted face, declaiming the war as the Fire Nation would like it to a full house. Vain, loud, oddly brave on a stage. Fights with a prop spear and the certainty that the audience is on their side.

creatures.name: Farmer
creatures.info: A farmer of the Earth Kingdom's plains, the Fire Islands' terraces or the colonies' fields, with a hoe, a pig and a son at the war. Suspicious of soldiers, generous with soup. Fights with the hoe and the dog, and tells the garrison whatever keeps the farm.

creatures.name: Fire Nation civilian
creatures.info: A townsperson of the Fire Islands: a fisher, a shopkeeper, a factory hand, a schoolteacher, in the plain red of the home islands with a son at the front and a portrait of the Fire Lord on the wall. Loyal, tired, curious about strangers. Fights only to run, and reports to the Domestic Forces afterwards.

creatures.name: Fire Nation firebender
creatures.info: A firebender of the Fire Nation in the army's armour or a noble's robes, drilled in the breath and fist forms from childhood, strongest at noon and under the comet. Proud, quick to anger, quicker to flame. Fights with blasts, whips and shields of fire, and is helpless on the Day of Black Sun.

creatures.name: Fire Nation noble
creatures.info: A noble of the Fire Nation in silk and gold, a topknot and a flame pin, with servants, a sedan chair and an opinion of the war shaped by the Royal Plaza's rallies. Courteous to rank, cold to the rest. Fights, if at all, with a hired guard and a word to the Domestic Forces.

creatures.name: Fire Nation soldier
creatures.info: A soldier of the Fire Army in red and black lacquered armour and the skull-faced helm, a spear or a sword in hand and a squad around him. He holds what the army has taken, checks papers, and obeys. Nonbender; fights in formation with spear and shield and calls for a firebender when the line breaks.

creatures.name: Fire Navy sailor
creatures.info: A sailor of the Fire Navy's iron cruisers, in the fleet's red with a cap and a short sword, coal dust in the creases. He coals, rows, hauls and boards, and talks more than he should in port. Fights with a cutlass and a belaying pin and gives ground on land.

creatures.name: Fire Sage
creatures.info: A sage of the Fire Sages in the tall red hat and robes of the temples, keeper of a flame, a record and a rite, who served the Avatar once and serves the Fire Lord now. Grave, formal, divided in private. Fights with ceremonial fire and the temple's mechanisms, reluctantly.

creatures.name: Flying bison
creatures.info: The great six-legged flying beast of the Air Nomads, the first airbender, which carried the monks between the temples and carries the last one now; Appa is believed the last of them. Loyal, gentle and ten tons. Fights with a tail blast of air and a landing.

creatures.name: Foggy Swamp bender
creatures.info: A waterbender of the Foggy Swamp Tribe in a leaf skirt, bending the water in vines and fog, convinced the swamp is one tree and that you are part of it. Friendly, strange, surprisingly dangerous. Fights with vine whips and a monster suit of living plants.

creatures.name: Freedom Fighter
creatures.info: A child or teenager of the Freedom Fighters with a weapon too big for them and a grudge bigger, living in the trees and striking from them. Brave, angry, quick to follow Jet and slow to doubt him. Fights from above with hook swords, a bow or a knife, and vanishes.

creatures.name: Giant rhinoceros beetle
creatures.info: A beetle the size of an ostrich horse with facial prongs, the beetle-headed merchants' beast of burden across the desert. Slow, strong and nearly impossible to hurt. Fights with the prongs and its weight.

creatures.name: Gilacorn
creatures.info: A small poisonous scavenging lizard of the Si Wong Desert, once a giant and a terror, now a nuisance that steals eggs and bites ankles. Fights with a venomous bite and a dash under the sand.

creatures.name: Hippo cow
creatures.info: A large omnivorous farm animal of the Fire Nation, its main source of meat and milk in the late war. Heavy, placid and immovable. Fights by sitting down on the problem.

creatures.name: Hog monkey
creatures.info: A pig-snouted primate of the Earth Kingdom and the Fire Nation, hard to tame and harder to ride, bribable with lychee nuts. Fights with a bite and a flung fruit.

creatures.name: Iguana parrot
creatures.info: A reptile bird of the Earth Kingdom's coasts, a sailor's and a pirate's favourite pet, perched on a shoulder and repeating what it hears. Fights with a nip and a scream for the crew.

creatures.name: Knowledge Seeker
creatures.info: A fox-like spirit assistant of Wan Shi Tong, travelling the world to collect books and scrolls for his library and helping its patrons find them, for a treat. Quick, silent, helpful if respected. Fights not at all; it leaves, and the owl knows.

creatures.name: Koala sheep
creatures.info: A woolly, round-eared grazing animal of the Fire Nation's hills, kept for wool and kept quiet. Docile, slow, easily lost. Fights only by bleating.

creatures.name: Koalaotter
creatures.info: A furry aquatic mammal of the North Pole and the Northern Sea, a swimmer among the ice with a koala's face. Curious and quick. Fights with a bite and a dive.

creatures.name: Komodo rhino
creatures.info: The Fire Nation's beast of burden and war, a horned reptile the size of a cart bred for the army, the cavalry and komodo sausages. Patient under a rider, murderous at the charge. Fights by goring and trampling and will not stop for a wall.

creatures.name: Kyoshi Warrior
creatures.info: A warrior of the Kyoshi Warriors in green armour, white face paint and the golden headdress, war fans in hand and footwork no army teaches. Disciplined, fierce, loyal to her band. Fights with the fans to block, cut and throw, and uses an attacker's strength against them.

creatures.name: Lion vulture
creatures.info: A maned vulture of the southern seas, fierce and aggressive, not native and spreading, captured for the circus when it can be captured. Fights with beak and talons in a dive.

creatures.name: Mechanist's engineer
creatures.info: An engineer trained by the mechanist, with calipers, soot and an idea, working on a war balloon, a submarine or a drill, for whichever side holds the workshop. Proud of the machine, careless of its use. Fights by starting the machine.

creatures.name: Merchant
creatures.info: A merchant of any nation with a cart, a stall or a ship's deck, a scale and a price for everything, including the price of not asking. Friendly to coin, cold to credit. Fights by hiring someone, or by selling the fighter's position to the other side.

creatures.name: Mongoose lizard
creatures.info: A giant reptile of the Fire Nation's jungles, domesticated as a fast mount that runs up walls and over water, a royal hunter's choice for a chase. Quick, vicious, obedient to a firm rider. Fights with bite and claw and a leap from above.

creatures.name: Northern waterbender
creatures.info: A waterbender of the Northern Water Tribe in the north's blue, drilled in Pakku's forms, strongest under the moon. Proud, traditional, unused to losing. Fights with waves, ice walls and the sea itself, and is lost without water.

creatures.name: Ostrich horse
creatures.info: The Earth Kingdom's mount and beast of burden, a tall two-legged bird that runs, climbs and kicks, ridden by soldiers, farmers and fugitives. Hardy and bad-tempered. Fights with a kick that breaks ribs.

creatures.name: Otter penguin
creatures.info: The four-flippered penguin of the South Pole's coast, in colonies, hunted for meat, kept as pets and ridden down the slopes by children with a fish for bait. Fights by sliding away.

creatures.name: Pirate
creatures.info: A pirate of the western seas off the captain's ship, in motley with a cutlass and an earring, selling curiosities on the deck by day and taking them back by night. Greedy, cheerful, easily insulted. Fights with cutlass, hook and the whole crew at once.

creatures.name: Platypus bear
creatures.info: A large bear with a bill and a flat tail, native to the Earth Kingdom's rivers and valleys, aggressive in the wild and prone to laying an egg when startled. Fights with claws and a swipe of the tail.

creatures.name: Polar dog
creatures.info: The Southern Water Tribe's dog, white, heavy-coated and loyal, a sled puller and a child's guard. Fights with a bite for its family.

creatures.name: Pygmy puma
creatures.info: A small cat of the Earth Kingdom's alleys, the self-appointed king of them, quick and fearless of anything smaller than a dog. Fights with claws and a yowl.

creatures.name: Rabaroo
creatures.info: A rare rabbit-eared hopping animal of the Earth Kingdom with a pouch, a sad sight in a zoo's cage and a quick one in the open. Fights with a kick and a bound.

creatures.name: Raven eagle
creatures.info: A black bird of prey that can be trained to intercept dragon hawks in the air and bring their scrolls down. Sharp, patient, expensive. Fights with talons in a dive.

creatures.name: Refugee
creatures.info: A refugee of the Earth Kingdom on the road to Ba Sing Se with a bundle, a family and a passport or the lack of one: a farmer, a deserter, a widow, a cabbage merchant. Hungry, hopeful, easily cheated. Fights to keep the bundle and runs for the ferry.

creatures.name: River spirit
creatures.info: A spirit of a river, benevolent while the river is clean and absent when it is not, which heals the sick who come to the water and haunts whoever fouls it. The Jang Hui's is the Painted Lady. Fights with fog, the river's water and fear.

creatures.name: Rough Rhino rider
creatures.info: A rider of the Rough Rhinos on a komodo rhino, each with his own weapon: chain, bow, explosives, a bender's fire. Paid by the job, loyal to the pay, gone by nightfall. Fights from the saddle at the charge and burns a town in an afternoon.

creatures.name: Royal Earthbender Guard
creatures.info: A guard of the Royal Earthbender Guards in green and gold at a palace door or a wall gate, reading passports and standing posts for a king he protects and never hears from. Formal, dutiful, uneasy. Fights with earthbending and a halberd and holds a gate to the last.

creatures.name: Saber-tooth moose lion
creatures.info: A large antlered predator of the southern Earth Kingdom's forests, vicious when threatened and worse when its cub is. Fights with antlers, teeth and a charge that breaks trees.

creatures.name: Sandbender
creatures.info: A bender of the Si Wong tribes in sand-coloured robes and goggles, on a sand-sailer or beside one, bending the loose sand the way no city earthbender can. Hospitable with water, hard about everything else. Fights with sand whips and a sandstorm, and leaves on the sailer.

creatures.name: Scholar
creatures.info: A scholar of Ba Sing Se University or a wandering one, in a green gown with scrolls and a map, looking for a ruin, a library or a fact. Excited, impractical, braver than sense. Fights by hiding behind the party and taking notes.

creatures.name: Screeching dodo
creatures.info: A small fluffy white bird of the Foggy Swamp known for a high ominous scream that sounds like something dying. Harmless, and the worst thing to hear at night. Fights not at all.

creatures.name: Serpent
creatures.info: The sea serpent of the East and West Lakes that the Serpent's Pass is named for, a creature long enough to wrap the pass's rock and tall enough to look over it. Territorial and quick. Fights with a crushing coil and a bite from the water.

creatures.name: Shirshu
creatures.info: A great blind tracking beast of the southern Earth Kingdom's underground, with a nose that follows a scent across a continent and a tongue that paralyses. Obedient to one rider. Fights with the paralysing tongue and a charge.

creatures.name: Southern Raider
creatures.info: A raider of the Southern Raiders in the unit's black armour and sea-wolf mask, off a ship that came in under its own soot. He takes who is on the list and burns the rest, and does not look back at the village. Fights with firebending and a boarding blade, in a rush up a beach.

creatures.name: Southern villager
creatures.info: A villager of the Southern Water Tribe at Wolf Cove, a child, a grandmother or a boy who calls himself a warrior, in worn blue, keeping a village the war emptied. Wary, warm, hungry for news of the men. Fights with a boomerang, a spear and the children's traps.

creatures.name: Spirit
creatures.info: A spirit of the Spirit World with no name a human knows, a shape that is almost an animal or almost a person, met on the spirit roads or in the fog. Curious, indifferent or angry, as it was made. Fights with whatever it is: wind, fear, a shape that changes.

creatures.name: Spirit World firefly
creatures.info: A firefly of the Spirit World that gives a bright bluish light, and whose light leads a walker to what they are looking for, if they follow. Fights not at all.

creatures.name: Temple settler
creatures.info: A settler of the mechanist's colony at the Northern Air Temple, an Earth Kingdom refugee turned engineer, in goggles and a leather apron, who has filled an airbenders' temple with pipes and gliders. Clever, cheerful, uneasy about the bargain. Fights with a wrench, a glider's dive and the mechanist's inventions.

creatures.name: Tiger seal
creatures.info: A striped seal of the South Pole's icy bays, the tribe's food and fur, quick in the water and heavy on the ice. Fights with a bite and a bull's charge on the shore.

creatures.name: Tigerdillo
creatures.info: A large armoured striped predator of the Earth Kingdom, extremely dangerous and rarely seen, a shell no spear opens. Fights with claws and a rolling charge.

creatures.name: Turtle duck
creatures.info: A small shelled duck of the ponds of the Fire Nation and the Earth Kingdom, fed bread by children and princes. Gentle, and fierce for its ducklings. Fights with a nip and a flap.

creatures.name: Turtle seal
creatures.info: A shelled seal of the ice caverns under the North Pole and the bergs of the Northern Sea, whose breathing holes lead into the city from below. Shy and armoured. Fights with a bite and a shell.

creatures.name: Two-headed fish
creatures.info: A mutated amphibious fish of the Jang Hui River, two-headed from the factory's waste, eaten by the village because there is nothing else. Sick, slow, strange. Fights with a bite that makes the biter ill.

creatures.name: Unagi
creatures.info: The enormous carnivorous eel of Kyoshi Island's bay, which fires jets of water at high speed and eats whatever rides the elephant koi. Fast, hungry, and a hazard to the harbour. Fights with the water jet and a bite the size of a boat.

creatures.name: Water Tribe warrior
creatures.info: A warrior of the Water Tribes in blue and fur with a bone club, a boomerang or a spear, and war paint for a fight, off a cutter or a canoe. Loyal, practical, funny when it is safe. Nonbender; fights with club and boomerang and with a plan.

creatures.name: Winged lemur
creatures.info: A small winged lemur of the air temples, critically endangered, energetic, a thief of fruit and a hero in small matters; Momo is the last known. Fights with a bite, a scratch and a distraction.

creatures.name: Wolfbat
creatures.info: A wolf-faced bat of the Earth Kingdom's caves, the Cave of Two Lovers above all, that comes in a shrieking cloud when a torch goes by. Fights with a bite and a swarm's confusion.

creatures.name: Yuyan archer
creatures.info: An archer of the Yuyan Archers in the red and black of the Pohuai Stronghold, face painted, bow strung, silent in the trees. He pins a target without killing it unless told to, and nobody sees him draw. Fights at range with pinning shots and falls back when closed with.

items.name: Abacus
items.info: A wooden counting frame with sliding beads. Merchants work out a price on it faster than any buyer can follow. 6 Pieces, sold at any Earth Kingdom market.

items.name: Acolyte's Flame Pendant
items.info: A small brass flame on a cord, given at the acolyte's oath.

items.name: Admiral's Flame Standard
items.info: A small standard of the admiral's flame, flown from his flagship.

items.name: Aide's Map Case
items.info: A leather case for a general's maps.

items.name: Air Nomad Head Shaver
items.info: A small curved blade of the kind the Air Nomads used to keep their heads bare and themselves closer to their element. A few still lie in the empty cells of the temples. Found, never sold: Southern Air Temple.

items.name: Air Nomad Leg Drapes
items.info: Brown trousers under a long split shirt whose drapes tuck into the boots. They catch the air as a young airbender falls and slow the drop. Found, never sold: Eastern Air Temple.

items.name: Air Nomad Monk Robes
items.info: Layered saffron under-robes with a long brown over-robe and a sash, the dress of a master airbender. A century of dust lies on the chests where the temple kept them. Found, never sold: Southern Air Temple.

items.name: Air Nomad Red Boots
items.info: Tall red boots made for the young airbenders in training, light and soft-soled for running on rooftops and rails. Found, never sold: Northern Air Temple.

items.name: Air Nomad Shawl
items.info: A loose orange shawl that catches the wind like a sail when its wearer falls. Novices wore them over yellow shirts. Found, never sold: Western Air Temple.

items.name: Air Temple Wind Chimes
items.info: Bronze chimes cast by the Air Nomads, still hanging in the empty temple. They ring in the lightest breeze, and the sound carries far down the cliffs. Found, never sold: Western Air Temple.

items.name: Airbender Staff
items.info: A wooden stave whose folded wings open into a glider. Closed, it fights like a quarterstaff and shapes an airbender's gusts; open, it rides the wind. The monks are gone, and their staves lie in the empty halls. Found, never sold: Southern Air Temple.

items.name: Airship Officer's Badge
items.info: A silver badge of an airship in profile, pinned at the collar.
items.where: Airship Officer, Fire Nation air force

items.name: Avatar Kyoshi Figurine
items.info: A painted wooden figure of Avatar Kyoshi with her fans, sold to visitors near the island's shrine. Islanders treat them with respect, and mocking one starts a fight. 5 Pieces, sold at Kyoshi Island.

items.name: Avatar Relics
items.info: Four old toys, a hog monkey, a hand drum, a clay turtle and a whirligig, laid out among thousands of others for Air Nomad children to choose from. The child who picks these four is likely the next Avatar. Taking them from the temple is sacrilege. Found, never sold: Southern Air Temple.

items.name: Ba Sing Se Passport
items.info: A stamped paper that lets a refugee board the ferry to the great city and pass the outer wall. The passport office checks faces against it, and a paper bearing the wrong name gets its holder arrested. 3 Pieces, sold at Full Moon Bay.

items.name: Balloon Crew Tag
items.info: A brass tag stamped with a balloon, carried by the crews.

items.name: Bamboo Canes
items.info: Seasoned bamboo stems for poles, ladders, fishing rods, scaffolds and bow staves. 1 Pieces, sold at any Earth Kingdom market.

items.name: Band Captain's Kyoshi Fan
items.info: A fan said to be cut to Kyoshi's own pattern.

items.name: Band Second's Headdress
items.info: The golden headdress of the band's second.

items.name: Betrothal Necklace
items.info: A choker with a stone pendant carved by hand. In the northern tribe a young man carves one for the woman he will marry, and once she wears it she is spoken for; old ones pass to granddaughters as heirlooms and are never sold. Found, never sold: Agna Qel'a.

items.name: Bison Whistle
items.info: A small wooden whistle whose note is too high for human ears. The Air Nomads herded their bison with such whistles, each keyed to one animal; merchants now sell them as worthless antiques, but sharp-eared animals still answer. 1 Pieces, sold at Seedy merchants pier.

items.name: Blasting Jelly
items.info: A sticky, pale jelly that blows apart dams, walls and the hulls of warships once fire touches it; the army uses barrels of it to blast out mountains. A pot destroys a barrier or a small building. Near a careless flame it takes the carrier too. 30 Pieces, sold at Seedy merchants pier.

items.name: Boat Captain's Compass
items.info: A bone compass of the southern cutters.
items.where: Boat Captain of the South, Southern Water Tribe

items.name: Boat Leader's Horn
items.info: A short bone horn that sounds a boat's landing.

items.name: Boat Mate's Whistle
items.info: A bone whistle of the crew's boats.

items.name: Bolt of Homespun
items.info: Rough undyed cloth from a village loom, enough for a shirt and trousers or a stout bag. 4 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Bolt of Silk
items.info: A bolt of dyed silk, enough for a fine robe. City tailors pay well for a good colour. 20 Pieces, sold at any Fire Nation market.

items.name: Bone Club and Boomerang
items.info: A Water Tribe bone club and a boomerang.

items.name: Bone-Headed Spear
items.info: A Water Tribe spear with a wooden shaft and a carved bone head, used to hunt seal and to hold a line on the ice. Light, cheap, and it never rusts on the ice. 14 Pieces, sold at any Water Tribe village.

items.name: Bone-Rimmed Tribal Shield
items.info: A broad Water Tribe shield of metal strapped to the left arm, reinforced with bone and marked with the moon. Southern warriors fight with spear in one hand and this in the other. 30 Pieces, sold at Wolf Cove.

items.name: Book of Clouds
items.info: A small tome of cloud shapes and what each foretells for the year, the book Makapu's fortuneteller reads the sky by. A fluffy bunny means doom and destruction; a bending arrow, a good harvest. Found, never sold: Makapu Village.

items.name: Bowl of Noodles
items.info: Hand-pulled noodles in broth with greens, ladled out at a counter for anyone with a few coins. Hot and quick, it restores a little strength. 2 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Brush and Inkstone
items.info: A writing brush, an inkstone and an ink cake in a cloth roll, for letters, maps and calligraphy. 4 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Bundle of Firewood
items.info: Split, dry wood tied with cord, enough for an evening's fire. On the ice and in the desert it is worth far more. 1 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Burner Hand's Gloves
items.info: A pair of scorched leather gloves with the air force's flame on the cuff.
items.where: Burner Hand, Fire Nation air force

items.name: Butterfly Swords
items.info: A pair of short single-edged blades whose hilt guards turn up so they can be flipped around the thumb. A street fighter's weapon: quick in a crowd, poor against a spear. 28 Pieces, sold at Lower Ring.

items.name: Cactus Juice
items.info: Juice squeezed from a desert cactus, the quenchiest thing in the sand. It slakes thirst, then does strange things: the drinker sees and says odd things for an hour unless a resolve roll holds the mind steady. 1 Pieces, sold at Misty Palms Oasis.

items.name: Canyon Walker's Rope
items.info: A rope the tribe's walkers carry.

items.name: Captain's Chart Case
items.info: A lacquered case holding a captain's charts and his commission.

items.name: Captain's Iguana Parrot Perch
items.info: A shoulder perch of the captain's pattern.

items.name: Captain's Palace Key
items.info: The great key of the palace's inner gate.
items.where: Captain of the King's Guards, Royal Earthbender Guards

items.name: Captain's Signal Horn
items.info: A short horn of lacquered brass that sounds a company's orders.

items.name: Cell Leader's Knot
items.info: A knotted green cord worn under the collar.

items.name: Chain Whip
items.info: Short iron rods linked by rings into a flexible whip with a dart at the tip. It wraps around a limb, hides as a belt, and lands a blow from beyond a sword's reach. 16 Pieces, sold at Harbor town.

items.name: Chained War Hammer
items.info: A sledgehammer on an iron chain that strikes at arm's length or swung out at range. An earthbender can drive it behind a thrown rock; bandits on the plains use it to smash doors. 36 Pieces, sold at any smith.

items.name: Chamberlain's Ring
items.info: A gold ring cut with the household's flame, shown to open any door in the palace.
items.where: Chamberlain's Hand, Fire Nation Royal Family

items.name: Champion's Belt of Earth Rumble
items.info: The belt the champion holds.

items.name: Chancellor's Seal
items.info: The seal of the university's chancellor.
items.where: Chancellor of the University, Ba Sing Se University

items.name: Chief's Dragon Scale
items.info: A scale of one of the last dragons.

items.name: Chief's Sand Standard
items.info: A standard of the tribes' chief, carried on the lead sailer.
items.where: Chief of the Tribes, Si Wong tribes

items.name: Chief's Whale Tooth Necklace
items.info: A necklace of whale teeth, the chief's.
items.where: Chief of the Southern Tribe, Southern Water Tribe

items.name: Chute Master's Hook
items.info: A hook for the delivery system's bins.

items.name: Circus Tent Peg
items.info: An iron tent peg of the circus.

items.name: Coin String Charm
items.info: Earth Kingdom coins with square holes, strung on a red cord and worn as a charm for prosperity. In a pinch, the coins spend. 3 Pieces, sold at any Earth Kingdom market.

items.name: Colonel's Contract Seal
items.info: The seal the band's contracts are closed with.

items.name: Colonial Clerk's Stamp
items.info: A brass tax stamp of a colonial office.

items.name: Commander's Sealed Orders
items.info: A set of orders under the Fire Lord's seal, the mark of the raiders' commander.

items.name: Commissioner's Seal
items.info: A seal in black iron, the mark of the home guard's command.

items.name: Commodore's Standard
items.info: A small flame standard of the air force, flown from the lead airship.
items.where: Airship Commodore, Fire Nation air force

items.name: Confidant's Blue Flame Pin
items.info: A pin of blue flame, the princess's mark.

items.name: Conical Straw Hat
items.info: A farmer's hat woven wide to throw as much shade as possible. It hides a face from a patrol as well as from the sun. 6 Pieces, sold at any Earth Kingdom market.

items.name: Constable's Whistle
items.info: A steel whistle of the Domestic Forces' pattern on a red cord.

items.name: Copyist's Brush Set
items.info: A set of fine brushes in a bamboo case.

items.name: Council Clerk's Brush
items.info: A brush with the council's mark on the handle.

items.name: Council Runner's Pass
items.info: A green paper pass with the council's five seals.

items.name: Council Secretary's Seal
items.info: The seal that closes the council's orders.

items.name: Councillor's Clean Sash
items.info: A white sash of the tribe's council.

items.name: Councillor's Crown Pin
items.info: A pin of Omashu's crown, worn by its councillors.

items.name: Councillor's Moon Pendant
items.info: A carved moon pendant of the chief's council.

items.name: Court Earthbender's Sash
items.info: A green sash of Omashu's court.

items.name: Crescent Jii
items.info: A halberd-spear with a crescent moon blade on one side, good against foot soldiers and riders alike. Racks of them stand in the battery armouries, and a few go missing every season. Found, never sold: Crater Rim Batteries.

items.name: Cutpurse's Hook Knife
items.info: A small hooked knife for purse strings.

items.name: Dai Li Captain's Green Seal
items.info: A green jade seal of the agents' command.

items.name: Dai Li Initiate's Hat
items.info: The conical hat of the agents.

items.name: Dai Li Robe
items.info: A long dark-green court robe with an earth-symbol rank square and deep sleeves that hide binding chains. In the city, people step out of its way. Found, never sold: Lake Laogai.

items.name: Dai Li Rock Gloves
items.info: A pair of the agents' stone gloves.

items.name: Dai Li Stone Shoes
items.info: Shoes soled with earth that let an agent slide along the ground and cling to walls and ceilings. Only an earthbender can use them; anyone else just has heavy shoes. Found, never sold: Lake Laogai.

items.name: Desert Head Wrap
items.info: Long strips of tan cloth wound over the head and across the mouth in the sandbender way. It keeps sand out of the hair and nose and heat off the skull. 8 Pieces, sold at Misty Palms Oasis.

items.name: Desert Ninjato
items.info: A straight sword with a square grip and guard, light enough to draw fast. Oasis cantina keepers slice fruit and ice with a pair of them, and use them on drunks who reach over the bar. 26 Pieces, sold at Misty Palms Oasis.

items.name: Director's Prompt Book
items.info: The director's book of every play the troupe has staged.
items.where: Director of the Players, Ember Island Players

items.name: Disguise Kit
items.info: Face paint, a hat, and a change of clothes in another nation's colours. The wearer blends into a foreign crowd as long as they do not talk too much. 10 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Dried Fruit String
items.info: Dried persimmons and plums threaded on a cord. They last for months in a pack and give a quick lift of strength on a climb. 1 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Dried Seal Blubber
items.info: A strip of tiger seal blubber from the southern bays, dried for the hunt. It is food on a long trip and fuel in a pinch, burning with a smell some find appetising. Eaten, it warms and fills. 2 Pieces, sold at any Water Tribe village.

items.name: Driver's Tank Crank
items.info: A crank of the princess's tank train.

items.name: Dual Broadswords
items.info: Two moderately curved, single-edged blades that sheathe together in one scabbard and are meant to fight as one weapon. Used in the Fire Nation and the Earth Kingdom alike; they chop and slash well and let a firebender fight without fire. 48 Pieces, sold at Shu Jing.

items.name: Dune Rider's Goggles
items.info: A pair of the tribes' dark goggles.

items.name: Earth Army Boots
items.info: Heavy boots of the kind nonbending soldiers wear on the march. Earthbenders scorn them, because they cut off the feel of the ground. 10 Pieces, sold at any Earth Kingdom market.

items.name: Earth Captain's Seal
items.info: A jade seal that stamps a captain's orders.
items.where: Earth Captain, Military of the Earth Kingdom

items.name: Earth General's Banner
items.info: A small green banner of the Earth Kingdom's generals.
items.where: Earth General, Military of the Earth Kingdom

items.name: Earth Kingdom Conical Helm
items.info: A wide-brimmed conical war hat with a small spike at the crown, worn over a cloth headdress. Its slope sheds a fire blast, and a soldier can crouch under it like a shield. 16 Pieces, sold at Outer Wall.

items.name: Earth Kingdom Guan Dao
items.info: A heavy pole weapon with a broad curved blade and a counterweighted butt. Dojo masters teach it in the mountains; it sweeps a ring clear around the wielder but is slow to turn. 44 Pieces, sold at Gaoling.

items.name: Earth Kingdom Jian
items.info: A straight double-edged sword of the Earth Kingdom pattern.

items.name: Earth Kingdom Lamellar
items.info: Layered green and brown plates over a quilted coat, the uniform armour of the Earth Kingdom's soldiers. Nonbenders wear the full set; benders strip it down for movement. 50 Pieces, sold at General Fong's fortress.

items.name: Earth Kingdom Road Map
items.info: A painted map of the kingdom's main roads, rivers and towns. Where the war has moved the lines, it is years out of date. 6 Pieces, sold at any Earth Kingdom market.

items.name: Earth Kingdom Shin Guards
items.info: Green lower-leg plates worn over gray trousers. Bending soldiers who go barefoot still keep their shins covered. 12 Pieces, sold at Pass Southern Gate.

items.name: Earth Kingdom Tower Shield
items.info: A tall wooden shield faced with bronze and painted green, made to stand in a wall of others along a rampart. It is heavy to march with and blunts both arrows and fire. 28 Pieces, sold at Outer Wall.

items.name: Earth Lieutenant's Helm
items.info: The conical helm of an Earth Kingdom officer.
items.where: Earth Lieutenant, Military of the Earth Kingdom

items.name: Earth Private's Green Token
items.info: A green clay token stamped with the Earth Kingdom's seal.

items.name: Earth Sergeant's Shoulder Plate
items.info: A green shoulder plate with the army's badge.
items.where: Earth Sergeant, Military of the Earth Kingdom

items.name: Elder's Staff of the Gan Jin
items.info: The elder's walking staff, carved and polished.

items.name: Elder's Staff of the Zhang
items.info: The elder's walking staff, scarred and unpolished.

items.name: Elephant Koi Oil
items.info: A small cask of oil rendered from elephant koi blubber, shipped from Kyoshi Island to every port. It burns clean in lamps and keeps leather and iron supple. 3 Pieces, sold at Kyoshi Island.

items.name: Ember Island Shell Necklace
items.info: A string of pink shells sold to holidaymakers on the island's beaches. It says the wearer has spent a pleasant summer at the resort. 2 Pieces, sold at Ember Island.

items.name: Fan Bearer's Paint Box
items.info: A box of the warriors' white, red and black.

items.name: Fellow's Green Gown
items.info: The green gown of the university's fellows.
items.where: University Fellow, Ba Sing Se University

items.name: Fever Tea
items.info: A bitter brew of willow bark and mountain herbs. A cup every few hours brings a fever down over a day. 3 Pieces, sold at any herbalist.

items.name: Field Kama
items.info: A farmer's reaping sickle, its edge kept keen past what the harvest needs. Every farmhouse has two; in a raid, the farmers fight with them. 6 Pieces, sold at Farming village.

items.name: Field Scholar's Trowel
items.info: A small bronze trowel with the university's mark.
items.where: Field Scholar, Ba Sing Se University

items.name: Fire Army Enlistment Tag
items.info: A stamped iron tag on a cord that every private carries.

items.name: Fire Army Gauntlets
items.info: Black leather gauntlets with red plates over the backs of the hands, open at the palm so a bender can throw fire. 14 Pieces, sold at Capital Drill Ground.

items.name: Fire Army Greaves
items.info: Red and black thigh and shin plates on a belted skirt of lamellar. They match the Fire Army's plate and are sold to recruits whose own were lost. 24 Pieces, sold at Capital Drill Ground.

items.name: Fire Army Helm
items.info: A red and black infantry helmet with a flared neck guard and cheek plates. Soldiers leave them on the field, and travellers in occupied country know to pick one up. Found, never sold: Pohuai Stronghold.

items.name: Fire Army Plate
items.info: Red and black lamellar plate over a padded coat, the standard armour of the Fire Army's infantry. Fresh suits leave the factory by the wagonload, and a few fall off the wagons. Found, never sold: Fire Nation Army factory.

items.name: Fire Army Sword
items.info: The standard long-bladed sword of Fire Nation infantry, plain and well tempered. The drill ground's quartermaster sells spares to anyone with enlistment papers or a convincing story. 30 Pieces, sold at Capital Drill Ground.

items.name: Fire Flakes
items.info: A paper cone of red, spiced flakes, the snack every Fire Nation child grows up on. They burn the mouth of anyone raised elsewhere, and a handful wakes a drowsy eater. 1 Pieces, sold at any Fire Nation market.

items.name: Fire Nation Buckler
items.info: A small round iron buckler with a flame boss, light enough to fight with a single sword. Marines and duelists carry it. 20 Pieces, sold at Fire Nation bazaar.

items.name: Fire Nation Dadao
items.info: A heavy, single-edged broadsword with a wide blade that swells toward the tip. Some Fire Army soldiers favour it for its chopping weight; it needs both hands to recover after a missed cut. 38 Pieces, sold at Fire Nation bazaar.

items.name: Fire Nation Silk Painting
items.info: A hanging scroll of a volcano at dawn, brushed on silk by a court-trained painter. Noble houses hang such scrolls in their halls; one in an Earth Kingdom home would draw questions. 50 Pieces, sold at Fire Nation Capital.

items.name: Fire Navy Deck Armor
items.info: Lighter black-and-red plate cut for climbing rigging and ladders, with a short skirt that will not drag a sailor under if he goes over the rail. 40 Pieces, sold at Harbour Quarter.

items.name: Fire Navy Deck Boots
items.info: Black boots with grooved soles that grip a wet steel deck. Sailors buy new pairs at the harbour before a long cruise. 12 Pieces, sold at Harbour Quarter.

items.name: Fire Navy Deck Token
items.info: A stamped iron disc on a cord that marks a sailor of the fleet.

items.name: Fire Sage's Red Hat
items.info: The tall red hat of a sage of the temples.

items.name: Firebender's Skull Mask
items.info: A protective face guard shaped like a skull, part of the armour issued to Fire Army benders. It covers the face in the heat of an exchange and frightens enemies before a flame is thrown. Found, never sold: Crater Rim Batteries.

items.name: Firecrackers
items.info: A string of red paper firecrackers for festivals. Lit, they crack and flash loud enough to scatter animals and startle a crowd for a moment. 2 Pieces, sold at any Fire Nation market.

items.name: First Mate's Cutlass
items.info: A notched cutlass of the crew.

items.name: Fishing Tackle
items.info: A rod, line, bone hooks and a little box of bait. With patience it puts a fish on the fire by any river or shore. 3 Pieces, sold at any port.

items.name: Flame Keeper's Taper
items.info: A lacquered taper that lights a temple's flame.

items.name: Flame Topknot Ornament
items.info: A gilded band with a small flame worked on it, worn on a Fire Nation topknot. Commoners tie plain cloth; this kind marks a noble house, and only the royal family wear pronged crowns. 30 Pieces, sold at Fire Nation Capital.

items.name: Flotilla Captain's Flame Lamp
items.info: A signal lamp of the raiders' pattern.

items.name: Fog Walker's Lantern
items.info: A lantern that burns swamp gas.

items.name: Freedom Fighter's Wheat Stalk
items.info: A stalk of wheat for the teeth, the band's habit.

items.name: Frozen Wood Frogs
items.info: Palm-sized brown frogs that freeze themselves through the winter at the bottom of a swamp, coated in a substance their skin makes. That coating cures a head cold: the sick person sucks on a frozen frog until the illness passes. 4 Pieces, sold at any herbalist.

items.name: Fur-Lined Mukluks
items.info: Soft seal-hide boots lined with fur and tied below the knee. The Water Tribes walk the ice in them for days. 10 Pieces, sold at any Water Tribe village.

items.name: Fur-Trimmed Leggings
items.info: Close-fitting breeches lined and trimmed with fur, worn under the parka by Water Tribe men and women alike. 8 Pieces, sold at Canal Market.

items.name: Gan Jin Washed Cloth
items.info: A spotless cloth of the tribe's pattern.

items.name: Garrison Officer's Red Armband
items.info: A red armband of the colonial garrisons.

items.name: Gate Keeper's Stamp
items.info: A brass passport stamp of the walls.

items.name: General's War Fan
items.info: A red and gold war fan, the mark of a general's command.

items.name: Ginseng Tea
items.info: Dried ginseng root brewed into a bitter, earthy tea that old men swear by. A cup restores a little stamina after a long day. 3 Pieces, sold at any herbalist.

items.name: Glider
items.info: A light wing of cloth on a wooden frame, built after the old Air Nomad gliders left lying about the temple. Strapped on, it lets someone who cannot bend air ride the wind down from a height. Found, never sold: Northern Air Temple.

items.name: Gold Bangle
items.info: A heavy bangle of Fire Nation gold, the kind noble ladies wear to court. It speaks of a good family before its wearer does. 35 Pieces, sold at Fire Nation Capital.

items.name: Gold Ingot
items.info: A small boat-shaped ingot of Earth Kingdom gold, used for great payments and seldom seen outside the rich rings. Money changers anywhere in the kingdom accept it. 120 Pieces, sold at Upper Ring.

items.name: Governor's Flame Banner
items.info: A small banner of a colony's governor, the Fire Lord's flame over the colony's mark.

items.name: Grand Lotus's Lotus Crown
items.info: A white lotus of carved bone, the Grand Lotus's mark.

items.name: Grappling Hook
items.info: A three-tined iron hook on a knotted line. Thrown over a wall or a ship's rail, it gives a climber a way up. 6 Pieces, sold at any smith.

items.name: Great Sage's Scroll Case
items.info: A sealed case for the sages' records.

items.name: Green Hair Claws
items.info: A pair of wide green claws worn on top of the head in line with the ears, as Ba Sing Se's officials and society ladies wear them. Worn well, they tell a doorman the wearer belongs inside. 15 Pieces, sold at Upper Ring.

items.name: Guard Lieutenant's Sash
items.info: A gold sash worn over green armour.

items.name: Guardian's Banyan Leaf
items.info: A great leaf of the banyan, the guardian's mark.
items.where: Guardian of the Banyan, Foggy Swamp Tribe

items.name: Guide's Green Robe
items.info: The green robe of the city's guides.

items.name: Haiku Novice's Fan
items.info: A paper fan with the society's seventeen marks.

items.name: Hand Wraps
items.info: Cloth wraps for the fists, weighted at the knuckles.

items.name: Handcuffs
items.info: Iron cuffs on a short chain for binding a prisoner's hands, as prison guards use; older Earth Kingdom sets add chains that bind the whole body. They hold anyone who cannot bend, though a firebender can heat them. 6 Pieces, sold at any smith.

items.name: Handler's Lamp Key
items.info: A key to the room under the lake.

items.name: Head of Cabbage
items.info: A firm green cabbage, the cheapest vegetable on any cart. Raw or boiled it feeds one person; whole carts of them have a way of being overturned when trouble rides through a market. 1 Pieces, sold at any Earth Kingdom market.

items.name: Head's Grand Secretariat Seal
items.info: The seal of the grand secretariat of Ba Sing Se.
items.where: Head of the Dai Li, Dai Li

items.name: Headliner's Painted Banner
items.info: A banner of the fighter's ring name.

items.name: Healer's Satchel
items.info: A leather bag of needles, thread, splints, bandages and dried herbs, a village healer's kit. In trained hands it closes wounds and sets bones. 15 Pieces, sold at any herbalist.

items.name: Healing Salve
items.info: A tin of waxy green salve for cuts and burns, including the burns soldiers bring home from the front. Rubbed in and bound, it heals a light wound and keeps it from festering. 6 Pieces, sold at any herbalist.

items.name: Hemp Rope
items.info: Fifty paces of twisted hemp rope. It ties up a boat, a bundle or a prisoner, and gets a careful climber down a cliff. 2 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Herbal Poultice
items.info: Crushed herbs bound in cloth, warmed and pressed on a bruise or sprain. Left on for an hour it brings down swelling and eases pain; it does nothing for a deep wound. 4 Pieces, sold at any herbalist.

items.name: High Sage's Crown Tongs
items.info: The tongs that set the Fire Lord's crown in his topknot.

items.name: Hippo Cow Steak
items.info: A cut from a hippo cow, one of the Fire Nation's main sources of meat and milk, seared to order at the bazaar's meat stalls. Even the beast eats meat, the butchers like to say. A heavy meal that restores strength. 4 Pieces, sold at Fire Nation bazaar.

items.name: Hook Swords
items.info: A matched pair of tiger blades: a hooked tip, a crescent guard over the fist and a spike at the butt. They parry, trip ankles and pull blades away, and a nimble wielder can hook branches and swing through the trees. 70 Pieces, sold at Omashu.

items.name: Hostess's Tea Set
items.info: A small tea set with the society's crest.

items.name: Household Guard's Gorget
items.info: A black gorget edged in gold, worn by the household's guards.
items.where: Household Guard, Fire Nation Royal Family

items.name: Hunting Bow
items.info: A horn-backed bow and a quiver of arrows.

items.name: Inspector's Warrant Plate
items.info: A brass plate stamped with the Fire Lord's flame and an inspector's number.

items.name: Iron Ingot
items.info: A bar of smelted iron ready for the forge. A smith turns a couple of them into a blade or a set of tools. 8 Pieces, sold at any smith.

items.name: Iron Parrying Fan
items.info: A folding fan with iron ribs and lacquered silk, carried as an ornament until a blade has to be caught. It turns a cut aside and snaps shut on a wrist. 24 Pieces, sold at Upper Ring.

items.name: Jade Badgermole Carving
items.info: A palm-sized badgermole carved from green jade by a master of the great city. Collectors in the Upper Ring trade such pieces as readily as coin. 80 Pieces, sold at Upper Ring.

items.name: Jade Ring
items.info: A ring cut from a single piece of green jade. Earth Kingdom merchants read it as the sign of a buyer with money. 25 Pieces, sold at Upper Ring.

items.name: Jailer's Chi Chart
items.info: A chart of the body's chi paths, Ty Lee's.

items.name: Jang Hui Clams
items.info: Blistered brown clams dug from the river bed below the factory and sold cheap on the village's stilt walks. The shells hold mud, weed and dead bugs along with the meat. They fill a belly, but the eater may need a stamina roll to keep them down. 1 Pieces, sold at Jang Hui.

items.name: Jasmine Tea
items.info: Loose jasmine leaves and blossoms, steeped in water just off the boil. A cup calms the nerves and clears a tired head before a hard conversation. 2 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Jelly Candy
items.info: Sweet fruit jelly in little pots, a treat for children. Keep it shelved well apart from blasting jelly, which looks much the same. It lifts a sour mood. 1 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Jennamite
items.info: A lump of creeping crystal, a rock candy that grows fast over any living thing it touches until the victim is encased; the kingdom's security forces were said to use it on spies. Broken off, it is a sweet snack. It pins a captive for an hour. 12 Pieces, sold at Omashu.

items.name: Joo Dee's Name Badge
items.info: A badge reading Joo Dee, the same as every other.

items.name: Judge's Ink Stone
items.info: An ink stone of the society's judges.

items.name: Keeper's Feed Bag
items.info: A feed bag with the circus's mark.

items.name: Keeper's Flame Bowl
items.info: A clay bowl for carrying the eternal flame.

items.name: Keeper's Lotus Scroll
items.info: A scroll of the order's teaching in a lotus case.

items.name: Keeper's Rule Scroll
items.info: A scroll of the tribe's rules.
items.where: Keeper of the Rules, Gan Jin

items.name: King's Hand's Ring
items.info: A ring of Omashu stone, the king's hand's mark.

items.name: Koi Charm
items.info: A small carved elephant koi on a cord, worn by Kyoshi Island's fishermen to bring the big fish to their nets. 3 Pieces, sold at Kyoshi Island.

items.name: Komodo Rhino Hide
items.info: A cured piece of komodo rhino hide, so tough that most blades break on it. Armourers stitch it into leather armour. 30 Pieces, sold at any Fire Nation market.

items.name: Komodo Sausage
items.info: A spiced sausage of komodo rhino meat, sold hot on a skewer from Fire Nation street stalls. Cheap, greasy and filling, it ends hunger fast. 2 Pieces, sold at any Fire Nation market.

items.name: Kukri
items.info: A heavy, forward-curved knife that is as much a tool as a weapon: it chops kindling, clears vines and settles a fight in the brush. 10 Pieces, sold at any Earth Kingdom market.

items.name: Kyoshi Folding Shield
items.info: A round shield that folds small on the forearm and opens in an instant. Locked edge to edge with others, a line of them turns a blast of fire; the island's warriors never part with theirs. Found, never sold: Kyoshi Island.

items.name: Kyoshi Katana
items.info: A long, slender, single-edged blade folded from carbon steel, the sword every Kyoshi Warrior carries beside her fans. The warriors seldom draw it, and they give it to no stranger. Found, never sold: Kyoshi Island.

items.name: Kyoshi Metal Headdress
items.info: A gilded metal crown band of the kind the island's band leader wears with her face paint. It marks a Kyoshi Warrior of rank; outside the island, anyone wearing it is asked where they got it. Found, never sold: Kyoshi Island.

items.name: Kyoshi Trainee's Green Sash
items.info: A green sash of the warriors' novices.

items.name: Kyoshi Warrior Kimono
items.info: An armoured green kimono embroidered with silk thread for the brave blood in a warrior's veins and a gold insignia for the honour in her heart. The warriors do not sell it; it must be given, or taken. Found, never sold: Kyoshi Island.

items.name: Kyoshi Warrior's Fan
items.info: A steel war fan of the island's pattern.

items.name: Lamp Oil
items.info: A stoppered flask of lamp oil, enough to keep a lantern going through a long night. It also burns well when thrown, which guards do not like to see. 1 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Lancer's Pennon
items.info: A red pennon for a lance, the band's mark.

items.name: Lead Player's Lacquered Fan
items.info: A lacquered stage fan, the lead's prop.

items.name: Leader's Twin Hooks
items.info: A pair of hook swords of Jet's own pattern.
items.where: Leader of the Freedom Fighters, Freedom Fighters

items.name: Lieutenant's Helm Crest
items.info: A brass crest for the helm, given at a lieutenant's commission.

items.name: Lieutenant's Hook Sword
items.info: One of the band's hook swords.

items.name: Lieutenant's Rampart Key
items.info: A key to the wall's inner stair.

items.name: Lieutenant's Saddle Plate
items.info: A brass plate for a rhino's saddle, the mark of a lieutenant.

items.name: Linen Bandages
items.info: Clean linen rolled tight for binding wounds. Applied well, a bandage stops bleeding and keeps a cut clean until it can be seen to. 2 Pieces, sold at any herbalist.

items.name: Lochaber Axe
items.info: An axe head mounted on a tall pole, with a hook on the back of the blade for dragging riders, shields and clothing. Earth Kingdom levies carry it because farmers already know the swing. 32 Pieces, sold at Omashu.

items.name: Long Spear
items.info: An ash spear with a steel head.

items.name: Lychee Nuts
items.info: A bag of sweet lychee nuts. People snack on them, and trappers bait snares with them because few animals can resist. 1 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Magistrate's Gavel
items.info: A black gavel of the colonial courts.

items.name: Marksman's Thumb Ring
items.info: A horn thumb ring cut with the Yuyan mark.

items.name: Mask Bearer's Skull Mask
items.info: The white skull mask of the Royal Procession.

items.name: Master's Lotus Teapot
items.info: A small teapot with a lotus on the lid.

items.name: Master's Throne Key
items.info: A gold key to the throne room's inner door, carried by the master alone.
items.where: Master of the Procession, Royal Procession

items.name: Master's Water Pouch
items.info: A sealskin pouch of the tribe's masters.

items.name: Member's Lotus Pouch
items.info: A pouch that holds the tile and nothing else.

items.name: Merchant's Seal Ring
items.info: A bronze ring with a carved seal face, pressed into wax to sign a contract. A trader without one is not taken seriously in the city's counting houses. 18 Pieces, sold at Middle Ring.

items.name: Mistress's Roster
items.info: The roster of every woman who has been Joo Dee.
items.where: Mistress of the Ambassadors, Cultural Ambassadors

items.name: Mistress's Scroll of Lines
items.info: A scroll of the society's best lines, kept by its mistress.
items.where: Mistress of the Society, Five-Seven-Five Society

items.name: Monk's Wooden Beads
items.info: A loop of large wooden beads of the kind Air Nomad monks wore about the neck. A few strings remain in the temple's cells; counting them slows the breath for meditation. Found, never sold: Southern Air Temple.

items.name: Monkey Statue
items.info: A stone monkey baring its teeth, with jewelled eyes and a necklace of rubies, sold among the pirates' curiosities. Whoever looks into those eyes too long finds it hard to look away. 60 Pieces, sold at Seedy merchants pier.

items.name: Moo-Sow Milk
items.info: A jug of sweet pig-milk from a moo-sow, the cow-pig that country towns keep in pens and prize for it. Drunk fresh it settles the stomach and restores a little vigour; left a day in the sun it does neither. 1 Pieces, sold at Farming village.

items.name: Naginata
items.info: A thick, slightly curved blade on a long wooden pole, a reach weapon that cuts in wide arcs. City guards drill with it in the yards behind the ring walls. 36 Pieces, sold at Middle Ring.

items.name: Navy Lieutenant's Sash
items.info: A red sash with the fleet's flame, tied at the lieutenant's commission.

items.name: Northern Fur Cloak
items.info: A heavy cloak of white fur with a purple-dyed lining, the cut favoured in the Northern Water Tribe. It sheds snow and doubles as a blanket. 26 Pieces, sold at Canal Market.

items.name: Northern Hunter's Bone Knife
items.info: A bone knife of the tribe's hunters.

items.name: Nunchaku
items.info: Two short sticks joined by a cord or chain. In trained hands they whirl and strike from odd angles; untrained hands mostly hit their own owner. 8 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Ocean Kumquats
items.info: Small bright fruit from the island shores, tart enough to make a face. Cooks squeeze them over seafood; eaten whole, they refresh a tired body. 1 Pieces, sold at any Fire Nation market.

items.name: Officer's Shoulder Mantle
items.info: A round shoulder cloth that gives the wearer the spiked silhouette of Fire Nation officers and nobles. It is mostly for show, but soldiers stand straighter when they see one. 26 Pieces, sold at Fire Nation Capital.

items.name: Omashu Bender's Tunic
items.info: A long yellow tunic with a green shawl and an earth-symbol belt buckle, worn by the earthbending soldiers who guard the gates and run the city's chutes. It leaves the limbs free for stances. 22 Pieces, sold at Omashu.

items.name: Omashu Gate Token
items.info: A stone token of the city's gate.

items.name: Orb Keeper's Replica
items.info: A small painted ball, the sacred orb's likeness.

items.name: Pai Sho Set
items.info: A round board of coloured squares and a bag of carved tiles. Pai Sho is played everywhere, each culture by its own rules; legend says spirits handed it down to teach patience and humility. 12 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Painted Lady Statuette
items.info: A small carved figure of the river spirit in her wide hat, kept in Jang Hui shops and homes. Villagers set them out in the hope that their guardian has not forgotten them. 3 Pieces, sold at Jang Hui.

items.name: Palace Guard's Breastplate Badge
items.info: A gold badge of the Earth King's seal.

items.name: Palace Page's Pin
items.info: A small flame pin in red enamel that marks a page of the royal household.

items.name: Paper Lantern
items.info: A paper lantern with a candle cup and a carrying stick. It lights a path for a few hours and shows the whole street where its carrier is. 2 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Pathfinder's Cord
items.info: A green cord worn at the wrist by the archers who scout.

items.name: Performer's Pink Sash
items.info: A pink sash of the circus's acrobats.

items.name: Petty Officer's Whistle
items.info: A brass whistle of the fleet's pattern, worn at the throat.

items.name: Pieces
items.info: Coin, counted in pieces: a copper piece is one, a silver ten, a gold a hundred. The Earth Kingdom's coins are round with a square hole and string together; the Fire Nation's ban come angular in copper, pentagonal in silver and slit in gold; the Water Tribes trade blue rings that some Earth Kingdom towns refuse. Every market counts in pieces.

items.name: Pilot's Goggles
items.info: Brass-rimmed goggles of the balloon pilots' pattern.
items.where: Balloon Pilot, Fire Nation air force

items.name: Pipa
items.info: A four-stringed lute with a pear-shaped body, played on music nights aboard ships and in village squares alike. 15 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Pirate Crossbow
items.info: A bow mounted on a wooden stock with a trigger and a quiver of short bolts. River pirates favour it because anyone can aim it after an afternoon; reloading is slow. 45 Pieces, sold at Seedy merchants pier.

items.name: Pirate's Earring
items.info: A brass earring of the crew.

items.name: Plague Painter's Pot
items.info: A pot of the purple make-up the plague is painted with.

items.name: Platinum Ingot
items.info: An ingot of platinum, purer and lighter to carry than gold, the rarest and most valuable money in the Earth Kingdom. Few outside the palace and the great houses have ever held one. 300 Pieces, sold at Upper Ring.

items.name: Player's Paper Mask
items.info: A paper mask of the troupe's pattern.

items.name: Players' Spear Prop
items.info: A painted wooden spear of the troupe's back row.

items.name: Poison Knife
items.info: An assassin's knife with a vial of poison hidden in the hollow handle and spikes that sit between the fingers. A cut carries the poison in, and the narrator decides how sick the wound makes its victim. Found, never sold: Seedy merchants pier.

items.name: Pork Dumplings
items.info: Dumplings pleated by hand and steamed by the dozen at a Lower Ring stall. A plate is the cheapest full meal in the city. 2 Pieces, sold at Lower Ring.

items.name: Pot Keeper's Ladle
items.info: A dented ladle of the tribe's pot.

items.name: Procession Captain's Flame Helm
items.info: The crested helm of a captain of the guard.

items.name: Procession Gate Token
items.info: A black iron token of the guard, shown at the palace gates.

items.name: Promoter's Gold Pouch
items.info: Xin Fu's gold pouch, or one just like it.

items.name: Pu Dao
items.info: An anti-cavalry pole weapon: a broad, curved blade on a long wooden shaft, made to meet a charging mount. The fortress quartermaster issues them to the pike lines and sells surplus to militias. 38 Pieces, sold at General Fong's fortress.

items.name: Raid Captain's List Case
items.info: A sealed lacquer case for the raid's lists.

items.name: Raider's Sea-Wolf Pin
items.info: A black pin of a sea wolf, worn by the raiders' crews.

items.name: Raw Jade
items.info: An uncut lump of green jade from the kingdom's mines. Carved, it becomes rings, seals and charms; Earth Kingdom nobles prize it above gold. 40 Pieces, sold at Mining village.

items.name: Red-Tufted Spear
items.info: A Fire Nation footman's spear with a red tuft beneath the head, there to draw an enemy's eye and to keep blood off the shaft. The colonies' garrisons sell their worn ones cheap. 18 Pieces, sold at Fire Nation colonial village.

items.name: Resistance Captain's Hook Sword
items.info: A hook sword of Omashu's guard.

items.name: Resistance Chalk Mark
items.info: A piece of green chalk for the resistance's wall marks.

items.name: Retracting Sai
items.info: A short dagger whose guard prongs fold flat into the hilt and snap out in the hand or in flight, so it turns from knife to sai mid-throw. Thrown edge-on, it slices through hanging cloth. 30 Pieces, sold at Fire Nation Capital.

items.name: Rhino Rider's Spur
items.info: A single iron spur of the band's pattern.

items.name: Rhino Sergeant's Horn
items.info: A rhino-horn drinking cup with the band's mark burned in.

items.name: Rice Ball
items.info: Sticky rice pressed round a pickle or a scrap of fish and wrapped in a leaf. It travels in a pocket and fills a stomach between meals. 1 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Rice Paper
items.info: A sheaf of thin paper for letters, posters, lanterns and kites. 2 Pieces, sold at any town market.

items.name: Rice Wine
items.info: A clay jar of cloudy rice wine. A cup warms the chest and loosens the tongue; the whole jar dulls pain and judgment alike. 3 Pieces, sold at Tavern.

items.name: Ring Fighter's Belt
items.info: A leather belt with a rock in the buckle.

items.name: Ring Master's Whip
items.info: The ring master's lacquered whip.

items.name: Roast Arctic Hen
items.info: A fat white bird of the northern ice, roasted whole in the city's kitchens and served with seaweed. A proper meal for a cold night; it restores strength. 3 Pieces, sold at Agna Qel'a.

items.name: Roast Boar
items.info: A haunch of boar from the kingdom's remote forests, the succulent meat that turns up at festivals and village feasts. Shared round a fire it feeds several people and lifts the spirits of everyone who eats. 6 Pieces, sold at any Earth Kingdom market.

items.name: Roast Iguana Seal
items.info: Meat of the green, spine-backed seal of the outlying islands. Sailors once rowed toward its calls thinking they heard a mermaid, and ate the singer instead. Roasted, it is a greasy meal that restores a little strength. 3 Pieces, sold at any Fire Nation market.

items.name: Roast Possum Chicken
items.info: The swamp tribe's everyday meat: a white-bodied bird with a possum's head and bare tail, hunted in the trees and roasted on a stick. Southerners say it tastes like arctic hen. A filling meal that eases hunger and a long day's fatigue. 2 Pieces, sold at Foggy Swamp Tribe.

items.name: Roasted Giant Fly
items.info: A fly the length of a forearm, hunted in the quagmires and roasted crisp over the cooking fire. Swamp folk eat it without a thought; guests need a moment. It fills an empty stomach and clears hunger's dizziness. 1 Pieces, sold at Foggy Swamp Tribe.

items.name: Rope Dart
items.info: A narrow iron dart on several yards of cord, thrown out and snapped back. It slices, binds an ankle, and coils up into a pocket. 14 Pieces, sold at Lower Ring.

items.name: Royal Armor
items.info: Black plate with scarlet detail and fine gold tracing, spanning the shoulders and the upper chest, with the national insignia beneath the throat in a shade reserved for the Fire Lord's kin. Wearing it outside that family is a crime. Found, never sold: Fire Nation Royal Palace.

items.name: Royal Courier's Seal
items.info: A brass seal with the Fire Lord's flame, carried on a chain under the collar.
items.where: Royal Courier, Fire Nation Royal Family

items.name: Rumble Challenger's Ticket
items.info: A stone ticket of the tournament.

items.name: Sack of Coal
items.info: Black coal from the mines. It burns hotter and longer than wood, and the war's forges and ships eat it by the ton. 2 Pieces, sold at Mining village.

items.name: Sack of Salt
items.info: Coarse sea salt boiled on the coast. Cooks need it, and so does anyone curing meat or fish for a voyage. 2 Pieces, sold at any port.

items.name: Sailer Captain's Rope
items.info: A length of the sailers' braided rope.

items.name: Sailer Pole
items.info: A sand-sailer's pole, iron-shod at both ends.

items.name: Salt Pork
items.info: Cured meat from a farm's hybrid pigs, the livestock rural kitchens in both the Earth Kingdom and the Fire Nation are built on. Salted hard, it keeps for weeks on the road; a slice with rice is a meal that restores a little strength. 3 Pieces, sold at Lee Family Pig Farm.

items.name: Sand Bender's Scarf
items.info: A long sand-coloured scarf of the tribes.

items.name: Scavenged Patchwork Armor
items.info: Fire Nation plates pulled from the dead, repainted, and stitched onto forest leathers. The Freedom Fighters wear such pieces; a stranger in it may be shot at by either side. Found, never sold: Gaipan.
