Masters are wary of a student who asks after the rare arts before the plain ones.

lore.name: Spirit lights
lore.info: On clear nights over both poles, curtains of light move across the sky, and the Water Tribes call them the spirit lights. The tribes hold that they are peaceful spirits dancing, and that while the lights shine, the world and the Spirit World are at peace with one another; to see them is to be reminded that a tribe is never far from its spirits. Sailors of every nation who work the polar seas know the lights too, and an old soldier who sees some sudden glow in the southern sky is apt to call it the celestial lights and go back to his tea. A stranger who mocks the lights, or calls them mere weather in front of an elder, will not be thanked for it.

lore.name: Spirit water
lore.info: Water drawn from a place where spirit runs strong carries more than water. The Northern Water Tribe's Spirit Oasis is the best known such place: a warm green garden in the heart of the ice where the pool never freezes, and its water mends hurts that ordinary healing cannot reach. Healers speak of spirit water as a last resort, kept in small sealed vials and spent only when a life is at stake. Anyone offering to sell spirit water in an Earth Kingdom market is almost certainly selling well water in a pretty bottle.

lore.name: Spirit World
lore.info: The Spirit World lies alongside the world of people, a plane of spirits where every wood, river and animal of the human world has something old and watchful behind it. Crossing over is rare. The Avatar is the bridge between the two worlds and can cross in spirit, leaving the body behind; a few others have done it by long meditation, and some have been carried across by a spirit as it passed, which is how people vanish from the edges of forests. The walls between the worlds are thinnest at the solstices, summer and winter, when spirits come through more easily. A spirit that takes a body in the human world gives up its immortality to do it. The dangers are told plainly to children: a body left behind lies helpless until its spirit returns; a spirit that wanders may not find its way back; and somewhere over there lives the face-stealer, who takes the face of anyone who shows him a feeling. Places like the Spirit Oasis stand close to the other side, and those who live near them treat them with care.

lore.name: Stupa
lore.info: A stupa is a domed shrine with a pointed spire, built wherever the land is thought to be strong in spiritual energy, usually far from towns, on a hilltop or high in the mountains. Some are monuments and some are buildings people can enter, and their shapes differ from nation to nation, though every one keeps the round dome and the spire. People come to them to meditate, and spirits are said to linger near them. The Air Nomads raised them, and so did the Earth Kingdom; a few serve as temples of the Avatar. A traveller should know that not every stupa in the mountains is what it seems. In the first years of the war, it is whispered, Fire Lord Sozin had false Air Nomad dwellings built in remote places, stupas and all, to lure out any airbender who had escaped, and some of those traps were never taken down.

lore.name: Summer solstice
lore.info: The summer solstice is the longest day of the year, the day the sun climbs highest. Like its winter twin it draws the human world and the Spirit World together, and in its days the border between them is almost nothing; a spirit-touched person, and the Avatar above all, may cross by meditation alone, or cross without meaning to. The solstices are written on the sanctuary floor of the fire temple on Crescent Island, and the sages who keep it watch the sun's place on those days. Summer is the Fire Nation's season, and firebenders feel the sun's strength at its height. Folk who fear the spirits keep their children close around both solstices; those who seek the spirits go to the old sacred places and wait.

lore.name: Surface-to-air rocks
lore.info: The watchtowers around the Earth Kingdom Royal Palace keep stacks of carved stone frusta, broad at one end and narrow at the other, by the dozen. The Royal Earthbender Guards launch them in teams of four, two to lift and two to throw, and flip each stone so its narrow face strikes first and is harder to dodge. Lined up and fired in quick succession, they stop men on foot and anything that tries to come in from the sky. No one approaches the palace grounds without leave; the stones are the palace's answer to anyone who tries.

lore.name: Swamp firefly
lore.info: In the Foggy Swamp lives an insect small enough to swat that can light up the whole clearing. Threatened, or calling a mate, the swamp firefly throws out a ball of white light so bright that onlookers have to turn their faces away, and for a moment it looks far larger than it is. Predators are dazzled and the fly escapes. Swamp people trap them in lanterns, and one will light a hut for a night. A camper who flails at one in the dark should be ready for what the flash shows: the swamp is crowded with eyes, and most of them are already looking at him.

lore.name: Ta Min
lore.info: Ta Min was a Fire Nation noblewoman, born to one of the richest families of the capital, and the wife of Avatar Roku. The young Roku loved her before he left to master the four elements, and when he came home a fully realized Avatar they married, with Sozin, by then Fire Lord and still his closest friend, as Roku's best man. The couple made a home on Roku's island among the villagers there. When the island's volcano woke in 12 BG, Roku stayed behind to hold back the lava so his wife and the villagers had time to reach the boats, and Ta Min watched from the water as he fought it. She survived him. Her name is still known among the capital's old noble families, if spoken more quietly now that the Fire Nation has turned against the Avatar.

lore.name: Tangle mine
lore.info: Chief Hakoda's warriors invented a mine the Fire Navy hates. A bamboo frame is covered in dried hide and packed with seaweed and skunk fish, then set floating in a channel. When a ship strikes it, the mine bursts: the seaweed wraps the propeller and stops the ship dead, and the smell drives the crew off the deck. The warriors call it the stink and sink, and it is cheap, light and very effective against steel ships. A Water Tribe band laying mines works at night and keeps upwind of its own handiwork.

lore.name: Tank train
lore.info: The tank train is the Fire Nation's answer to a land without roads: a heavy armoured engine that hauls cars of soldiers and cargo at speed across almost any ground, with no rails at all. The lead car holds the engine, fed by coal and firebending, and wears a sharp plough on its nose to batter through brush and boulders. Grappling-hook cannons sit on either flank, and the hauling cars behind can be coupled or dropped as a mission needs. The army calls it its finest all-terrain vehicle. Its plumes of smoke and steam show for miles, and an earthbender can feel it coming through the ground long before it is seen.

lore.name: Tea and the Teahouse
lore.info: Tea is the common drink of the Earth Kingdom and a favourite in the Fire Nation, and in most towns the teahouse is where news, gossip and Pai Sho happen. Earth Kingdom tea is brewed from many plants, jasmine, ginseng and lychee among them, while Fire Nation drinkers favour spiced tea. A good host pours before anything else is said, and a cup refused is a small insult. Old tea lovers insist that a cup is mostly patience and water, and only a little leaf. One warning travels with the trade: the rare white dragon bush makes a famous tea, and its look-alike, the white jade bush, is a poison that leaves the drinker covered in a burning rash. A traveller who brews from whatever he picks by the roadside should know the difference, or travel with someone who does.

lore.name: Terra Team
lore.info: An elite platoon of earthbenders under General Sung charged with defending the Outer Wall of Ba Sing Se, organised and coordinated, in the army's uniform with their own colour of helm and armour. They have never let anything through. A stranger sees them on the wall's top as small green figures; a soldier sees them as the best. One sworn to the Terra Team holds the wall, raises the stone, and rises by the platoon's trust, which is earned on the battlements.

lore.name: The legend of the two lovers
lore.info: Every bard in the Earth Kingdom knows the song. Long ago, two young people from villages at war, Oma and Shu, met on the mountain that divided their homes and fell in love, though their people forbade it. The badgermoles that lived in the mountain taught them to bend the earth, the first humans ever to learn it, and they used the gift to carve a labyrinth of tunnels where they could meet in secret. Then Shu was killed in the war. Oma, in her grief, raised such power that she could have destroyed both villages, and instead she declared the war over. The two villages built a city together in the lovers' memory and named it Omashu. The tunnels are still there and are called the Cave of Two Lovers, a maze no map can hold. The song's last line is its only advice: love is brightest in the dark, and the way out is to trust it.

lore.name: The library under the sand
lore.info: Scholars all over the Earth Kingdom tell of a library that holds every book ever written, kept by a great owl spirit somewhere in the Si Wong Desert. Most of them have spent their lives searching and believe it a fable. The few who have come back from it tell the same things: that only the top of one spire shows above the dunes, and the rest lies buried; that inside are halls of shelves without end and foxes that run errands for their master; that the keeper asks every visitor to add some knowledge to his collection before reading from it; and that he has grown suspicious of humans who come to learn how to win wars. The desert tribes know the way better than any scholar but rarely say so. A traveller who goes looking for it should bring water, a guide and something worth teaching.

lore.name: The oasis in the ice
lore.info: Deep within Agna Qel'a, in a cove behind the chief's palace at the foot of a waterfall, lies a garden that should not exist: grass, trees and flowers warm and green in the middle of the frozen north, growing plants found nowhere else in the tribe. The Northern Water Tribe holds that the spirits of the moon and the ocean came into the world near the beginning of time and made this place, and that their power keeps it warm. In its pond swim two koi, one white and one black, forever circling each other, push and pull, like the tides. Northerners say the moon was the first waterbender, and their ancestors learned the art by watching it pull the sea. Every full moon the tribe leaves food and gifts beneath the oasis gate in thanks for the spirits' protection. Outsiders are rarely let in, and nobody, northerner or not, so much as touches the fish.

lore.name: The tail of the largest whale
lore.info: Whaletail Island lies off the south-western coast of the Earth Kingdom, at the north end of the Southern Archipelago, and takes its name from its shape, which is the shape of a whale's tail lifted out of the sea. Water Tribe sailors have a story about it. They say the island really is a tail, the tail of the largest whale in the world, sleeping beneath the waves, and that this is why no whale is ever seen in the waters around it: the others keep a respectful distance. Southern sailors steer wide of it out of the same respect, and the Fire Nation, which keeps patrols in these waters, is not much welcomed there either. It is a long way from anywhere, many weeks' travel from Ba Sing Se.

lore.name: The unagi of Kyoshi Island
lore.info: In the bay off Kyoshi Island lives the unagi: a scaleless grey eel as long as a ship, with a spined crest on its head, sensory barbels either side of its mouth, sixteen pairs of hooked teeth and glands behind the jaw that shoot water out in a jet strong enough to knock a person off a rock. It eats anything in the water and hunts the elephant koi that young islanders like to ride. The villagers avoid that bay and threaten troublemakers with being fed to it; some criminals have been. It is afraid of anything larger than itself, and someone holding its barbels can steer it after a fashion. Visitors who want to ride the koi should ask a local first.

lore.name: The war as the Fire Nation teaches it
lore.info: Fire Nation children learn a different war from the one the rest of the world remembers. In their schoolrooms the Fire Nation is the greatest civilisation in history, and the war is its gift: a way of sharing its peace and prosperity with nations less fortunate. They are taught that the Air Nomads raised an army and plotted with the Avatar to rule the world, and that Sozin defeated that army bravely. They are not taught that the nomads were monks without weapons. Battles such as Han Tui are taught as lessons in cunning. A Fire Nation stranger abroad who repeats these lessons will be hated for it, and a foreigner in the Fire Islands who contradicts them will be reported.

lore.name: The war under Azulon
lore.info: Fire Lord Azulon reigned for most of the war, from 20 AG to 95 AG, and under him the Fire Nation's conquest became a patient grinding advance. His armies pushed east across the Earth Kingdom toward Ba Sing Se and his navy turned south, raiding the Southern Water Tribe again and again until its waterbenders were gone. Colonies grew in the occupied west and the colonists' children grew up there. The dragon hunts his father began went on until the last great dragon fell. Not everything went the Fire Lord's way: King Bumi made Omashu a fortress of resistance in the west, uprisings flared in the colonies, and the long assault on Ba Sing Se under his heir Iroh broke against the city after six hundred days. Azulon's portrait in the palace shows him standing over a great beast, the victories of his reign. He died in 95 AG, and his younger son, not his heir, was crowned.

lore.name: The war under Ozai
lore.info: Fire Lord Ozai has ruled since 95 AG, and the occupation has grown harder under him. Rebellion in the Earth Kingdom is put down without mercy; in many occupied towns earthbenders are seized and shipped to prisons at sea, where no earth lies within reach of their hands. Critics of the throne, at home or in the field, are silenced. In his war room generals plan as he pleases, and a prince who spoke against sacrificing a division of raw recruits was burned and banished for it. The Fire Nation holds most of the continent's west and north, the Earth Kingdom's armies are falling back toward Ba Sing Se, and the South has no benders left to fight. By this winter only the Northern Water Tribe, Omashu and the capital's walls stand between the Fire Lord and the end of the war, and Sozin's Comet returns next summer.

lore.name: The war's first twenty years
lore.info: Sozin's first blow fell everywhere at once. While the air temples burned, Fire Army landings on the western coast of the Earth Kingdom aimed to win a foothold on the continent and wreck the trading towns that fed the Earth King's armies. Battles such as Han Tui and Garsai won that foothold. At sea the Fire Navy beat the Water Tribes' fleets in a string of great battles, leaving the North to look to its own walls and the South open to whoever came. Sozin had aimed the whole stroke at one child, the new Avatar, and the child was never found among the dead; the old Fire Lord spent the rest of his life searching and died in 20 AG without an answer. His son Azulon took the throne and the war together.

lore.name: The warning at the pass
lore.info: At the gate to the Serpent's Pass, the narrow strip of rock between the East and West Lakes, stands a sign with the pass's name, and carved into one of the gateposts are two words: abandon hope. The pass was once the only road from the southern Earth Kingdom to Ba Sing Se, before the ferries began running across the lake, and the carving comes from those years. The path itself is straight; the name comes from the serpent that guards it, a creature as long as a ship that lives in the lake and rises to anything crossing above it. In places the path climbs high over the water between sheer cliffs; in one place it drops below the surface entirely. Refugees who can buy a ferry ticket take the boat. Those who cannot are told the story of the gate and decide for themselves.

lore.name: Theatre in the Fire Nation
lore.info: The Fire Nation loves its theatre, and nobles and peasants alike spend free evenings at plays. Acting is a respected profession even when a troupe is known to be bad. An old love story of dragons is staged every year in resorts and villages across the islands, and on Ember Island the Ember Island Players perform it at the island's only theater, to packed houses and no reputation for quality: grand speeches, loud effects and the same scenes butchered summer after summer. Noble mothers take their children to see them as a matter of course. Plays are free in their art but not in their politics: a play about the war is allowed on stage only if it ends in the Fire Nation's victory. A stranger in the audience laughs where the house laughs and keeps his opinions of the ending to himself.

lore.name: Top-knot
lore.info: The top-knot gathers the hair into a small bun at the crown, and it is the commonest hairstyle in the Earth Kingdom and the Fire Nation, for men and women of every class. Earth Kingdom knots are large and round, held by a plain ring of cloth or metal; generals and the rich wear elaborate rings and ornaments. Fire Nation knots are smaller and thinner, tied with red cloth or a tiny flame-shaped piece, and nobles fit headpieces to them. In the Fire Nation the knot is a sign of honour, almost sacred among the nobility. A firebender who loses an Agni Kai may shave part of his head, but leaves the knot; cutting it off entirely is akin to death, done only by those who turn their back on their country. Deserters cut theirs, and a man in the Fire Nation with no knot at all is looked at twice.

lore.name: Toucan puffin
lore.info: On the rocky coasts of the outer Fire Islands, toucan puffins sit in friendly, lazy crowds: black birds with white bellies, a blue breast and an enormous beak banded in red with a black tip. They can fly but hardly bother; they would rather sleep, hunt on the ground or crack fruit open with their beaks. Their favourite food is the cavehopper, so they gather near the mouths of sea caves. They let people walk right up, having learned that friendly birds get fed. The bright beak is for courting, and the males show it off at nesting time. A traveller hiding on those shores should know a crowd of puffins round him gives nothing away.

lore.name: Tracking with a shirshu
lore.info: The shirshu is a huge eyeless beast of the southern Earth Kingdom, like a mole the size of a cart, that lives in burrows and sees through a star of pink fleshy tendrils round its nose. It can follow one person's scent across stone, water and open ground over hundreds of miles. Its long whip of a tongue carries a venom that paralyses whatever it touches for minutes or hours, without lasting harm. Wild ones keep underground and away from people, and the war years have made them rarer still. The few that are tamed belong to bounty hunters and rich collectors, and their spit is made into paralysing darts. The beast's weakness is its nose: a hard blow or a strong perfume blinds it and can drive it into a panic.

lore.name: Tundra tank
lore.info: Tundra tanks are the Fire Army's newest war machines: squat, armoured hulls that crawl over ice and rough ground and carry firebenders inside, safe from arrows and thrown stone. Few have yet been seen in the field; they are the first tanks any army has built in numbers. Soldiers inside fire through hatches, and some hulls are fitted with a ballista for breaking walls. An Earth Kingdom picket that sees one should send a runner before it does anything brave, because spears do nothing to the plating.

lore.name: Turkey duck
lore.info: Turkey ducks are small white birds that wander the streets of Earth Kingdom towns like Makapu Village and the lanes of Ba Sing Se, a fan of tail behind them, a yellow bill, grey rings round the eyes and a strip of red wattle at the beak. They are scavengers and mostly gentle, and children chase them for fun. They also have a loud warble and a temper of their own. A turkey duck that is kicked, or hit by a kicked stone, flies straight at the culprit's head and pecks until he runs. Some people keep them as pets and name them. Villagers find it very funny when a grown traveller loses a fight with one.

lore.name: Ummi
lore.info: Water Tribe storytellers remember Avatar Kuruk, the Water Avatar before Kyoshi, as a man who took life easily until he fell in love. Her name was Ummi, and for her he meant to settle down. Before they could marry, the spirit Koh, the Face Stealer, took her and her face with her, to punish the Avatar for his carelessness. Kuruk spent the rest of his life hunting the spirit. The tale is told as a warning that spirits remember slights, that a careless Avatar makes enemies in the Spirit World, and that even an Avatar can lose what he loves. Mothers in the North add the lesson Koh teaches everyone: in front of a spirit who steals faces, show no face at all.

lore.name: Visions in the swamp
lore.info: Travellers who come out of the Foggy Swamp tell strange stories. The weather in it turns without reason, a fog lies over the water day and night, and people who spend a night in it see visions: faces of the dead, people they have lost, sometimes people they have never met. The swamp folk say the visions are real and that the swamp shows them on purpose, and that what it shows is the past, the present and what has yet to come. There is also the story of the swamp monster, a giant shape made of vines with a mask of leaves for a face, which rises from the water at anyone who harms the place. Earth Kingdom folk who live on its edges keep out. People who go in with an axe or a torch do not usually come out with either.

lore.name: Walrus yak
lore.info: Visitors who reach Wan Shi Tong's Library find the halls hung with mounted heads of creatures most people have never seen alive, hung high on the pillars. One is the walrus yak, with a walrus's tusks and snout under a yak's spiral horns and long white fur, which suggests it comes from somewhere very cold. Beside it hang a spider cat, all six red eyes and furry cat's ears on a spider's head, and a crocodile frog with a frog's broad skull, a crocodile's fangs and green fleshy frills. Nobody knows whether these beasts still live anywhere, or where the spirit's servants found them. A head very like the walrus yak's once hung among a pirate captain's curios, so collectors have seen one at least.

lore.name: War of Chin the Conqueror
lore.info: Some three hundred and seventy years ago, in Kyoshi's lifetime, a warlord named Chin raised an army against his own kingdom. He was cruel and proud; one tale has him striking down an emissary with earthbending just to show what he could do. His armies swept across the continent until only Ba Sing Se, behind its walls, and the small peninsula where the Avatar lived were left outside his rule. Rather than break himself on the capital, Chin marched to the neck of that peninsula and demanded its surrender. Kyoshi warned him she would not let him take her home. When he would not back down she entered the Avatar State, split the land from the continent and sent it drifting out to sea. Chin stood on the crumbling edge and refused to step back until it fell beneath him, and his war died with him.

lore.name: Warrior's wolf tail
lore.info: The warrior's wolf tail is the hairstyle of Water Tribe men: the hair pulled back and tied in a short queue behind the crown, not knotted on top of it. Young warriors shave the sides of the head and grow only the top; older men let the sides grow out until the tail reaches the shoulders or the middle of the back. The name matters to those who wear it, and calling it a ponytail is a quick way to annoy a young warrior. The style is close enough to a top-knot that a Water Tribe man can pass in the Fire Nation by retying his hair, which is worth knowing for anyone who must walk an enemy's streets with a southern face.

lore.name: Waterbending
lore.info: Waterbending was first learned from the moon, which pushes and pulls the sea, and the Water Tribe still honours it as the art's teacher. Water is the element of change and its season is winter. A waterbender turns an attacker's strength back on him, shifting from a whip of water to a wall of ice to a cloud of mist in a breath. The art grows with the night and swells under the full moon; a waterbender caught in the open at noon, far from any river, is weaker than at dusk on a frozen shore. The best can draw water from the air or from living plants. The Northern Water Tribe keeps the art strong behind its walls of ice. In the South, raids over the decades took nearly every bender away, and a southern child who moves water is now a rare thing and a dangerous one to own.

lore.name: Waterbending scroll
lore.info: Waterbending masters of the North set down their forms in illustrated scrolls: a figure drawn in pose after pose, from the beginning posture through strikes and turns, with the flow of water marked around it. A good scroll lets a bender with no teacher learn forms by copying the figures, which is why the northern tribe guards its scrolls and why they almost never leave the poles. Tribal tales say one old scroll was stolen long ago and has been sold from hand to hand since. A genuine scroll is worth a small fortune to the right buyer; many offered in Earth Kingdom ports are copies drawn by people who have never seen water bend.

lore.name: Waterbending training
lore.info: A waterbending student starts by streaming the water: drawing it up from a pool and passing it around the body, again and again, until the hands feel the push and pull the way the moon feels the tide. Breath comes first, because breath moves chi. Northern masters teach in large classes and test them in water duels, each winner facing the next student until someone goes down, which sorts a class by skill in an afternoon. Masters away from the poles teach resourcefulness instead: a bender in a dry land must find water in the air or in what grows. The Northern Water Tribe holds to an old rule that only men learn to fight with the art; its daughters who bend are sent to the healers' huts, and asking a northern master to teach a girl the water whip is the fastest way to be shown the door.

lore.name: Wei Jin
lore.info: Wei Jin is the patriarch of the Zhang. In their telling he was leaving his village when he found a Gan Jin man, Jin Wei, collapsed on the road with a sacred orb. Wei Jin tried to tend his wounds, but the fallen man begged him to carry the orb home for him instead. Wei Jin did, and the Gan Jin seized him at their border as a thief and gave him twenty years in prison. The Gan Jin tell it the other way round: a greedy coward who tripped their hero and stole their relic. A hundred years of hatred hang on that one afternoon, and both tribes teach it to their children word for word.

lore.name: Wheel of Punishment
lore.info: Chin Village sentences its convicts with a wheel. A guilty prisoner spins an upright painted disc, taller than a man, and the pointer at the top picks the sentence when it stops: a bed of nails, the whipping post, boiling in oil, a shark, a razor pit, a platypus bear, burning alive, or community service. The wheel is meant to deter as much as punish, and the village turns out to watch, since a spin is half sentence and half entertainment. The village honours the conqueror Chin as a great man and hates Avatar Kyoshi. A visitor who praises Kyoshi there may find himself at the wheel.

lore.name: Winter solstice
lore.info: The winter solstice is the shortest day of the year, and the most spiritual. As it nears, the line between the human world and the Spirit World thins: spirits cross over and act with great power, and people can pass into the Spirit World more easily, by their own gift or carried by a spirit. A village with an angry spirit in its woods fears the solstice more than any other day, because whatever has been taking its people grows bold in those days. The Fire Sages write the solstice on the sanctuary floors of their temples among the turning points of the year. A traveller who must cross haunted ground, or who has given a spirit cause to remember him, does well to settle the matter before the shortest day comes round.

lore.name: Wolfbats of the caves
lore.info: Wolfbats are wolf-sized cave beasts with a bat's leathery wings and face, a pig-like snout and sharp teeth. They roost upside down in big colonies by day, hunt at night and sometimes howl at the moon. The Cave of Two Lovers is full of them. Horrible stories are told about them, but they are mostly harmless to people unless surprised. Then a whole swarm takes off at once, which looks like an attack and can knock a careless climber off his feet. They are terrified of badgermoles, their only hunter, and anything that sounds like one sets them off. A light carried quietly through their caves is safer than a torch waved at them.

lore.name: Wood frog
lore.info: Along the western coast of the Earth Kingdom, the brown, palm-sized wood frog survives the winter by freezing solid at the bottom of a swamp. While frozen its skin sweats a coating that keeps the cold out, and that coating is a medicine: a person sick with a bad head cold or fever sucks on a frozen frog and the illness eases. Any herbalist will tell a traveller where the frogs lie. The catch is that they are useful only while frozen. Once they thaw they wake up and wriggle, the medicine is gone, and the patient generally spits the frog out. Gather plenty and get back quickly; winter is the only season for it.

lore.name: Wulong Forest
lore.info: The Wulong Forest is a wild stretch of the Earth Kingdom's western coast where hundreds of stone pillars rise straight out of the land, some higher than a temple tower, their tops crowned with trees and their feet lost in green forest and mist. It is called a forest for the pillars as much as for the trees. There are no roads worth the name: the ground between the columns is broken, steep and overgrown, and travellers lose sight of each other within a few steps. An earthbender finds the place full of stone to use; anyone else finds it a maze with no way to see out. Few people live near it, and those who do say it is a place to look at from a distance.

lore.name: Yuyan Archers
lore.info: An elite company of Fire Nation archers under the command of Shinu at the Pohuai Stronghold, who can pin a fly to a tree from a hundred paces without killing it, used for the stealthy missions where precision decides everything and counted among the Fire Nation's secret weapons. They took the Avatar alive in the winter of 99 AG. A stranger does not see them; an enemy sees one arrow. One sworn to the Yuyan Archers trains the eye and the stillness, goes where the colonel sends, and rises by the shot nobody else could make.

lore.name: Zhang
lore.info: An Earth Kingdom tribe that has feuded with the Gan Jin for centuries, driven from its lands by the war and bound for Ba Sing Se, rough, loud, generous and dirty, and proud of all four. They camp at the rim of the Great Divide and will not cross with the Gan Jin. A stranger is fed from the pot and told the feud; a tidy stranger is told it twice. One sworn to the Zhang eats, fights and laughs with the tribe, and rises by what they carry across the canyon.

starts.name: (Party) The Northern Air Temple
starts.info:
PARTY · Book One · 2-5 players · Aang, Katara and Sokka · guided
📍 Northern Air Temple, The Four Nations. One of the four Air Temples, on a peak of the Taihua Mountains along the continent's north coast, emptied in the Air Nomad Genocide and settled a generation ago by Earth Kingdom refugees under the mechanist after a flood took their village.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 9-24)

Aang wanted to see an Air Temple full of airbenders. What the party finds instead is a temple full of Earth Kingdom refugees, gliders, machines and a mechanist with a secret he does not want to talk about.
🎭 Teo, Male, a boy who cannot walk and lives at the Northern Air Temple with his father. Shaggy black hair, olive green tunic. A boy in a winged wheelchair diving off a mountain and laughing.

starts.name: (Party) The Old Masters' Camp
starts.info:
PARTY · After the comet · 2-5 players · Iroh · guided
📍 Agrarian Zone, The Four Nations. The farmland between the Outer Wall and the Inner Wall, fields and villages that feed the city, with Lake Laogai in the middle and the monorail crossing it on its piers.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 6-24)

On the day of the comet a handful of old masters took Ba Sing Se back in a single night. Now they sit in their camp on the farmland outside the walls, drinking tea and arguing over Pai Sho, and Iroh has asked the party to stay.
🎭 Bumi, Male, the king of Omashu. A cackling old king offering a guest a choice between three impossible tests.
🎭 Jeong Jeong, Male, the Deserter. Wild spiky shoulder-length white hair, ragged dark brown hooded robe. An old firebender in a hut in the forest, refusing a student who has come a long way.
🎭 Pakku, Male, the waterbending master of the Northern Water Tribe. Dark blue robe with a white fur collar. An old master refusing to teach a girl in front of a whole training ground.
🎭 Piandao, Male, the greatest swordmaster and swordsmith of the Fire Nation. Black high-collared robe with gold trim. A master swordsman at his gate, asking a stranger why he wants to learn.

starts.name: (Party) The Refugee Ferry
starts.info:
PARTY · Book Two · 2-5 players · Zuko and Iroh · guided
📍 Full Moon Bay, The Four Nations. A secluded cove on the eastern of the two lakes, south of Ba Sing Se, where the hidden ferry station takes refugees across the lake to the city.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 9-24)

The banished prince and his uncle are refugees now, wanted by their own nation and travelling under false names. The party has fallen in with them on the road to Ba Sing Se, and the ferry across the lake is the only way in.
🎭 Suki, Female, the leader of the Kyoshi Warriors of Kyoshi Island. Pale olive green kimono armour with a dark brown chest plate. A girl in white face paint teaching a cocky boy a lesson in her dojo.
🎭 The Passport Attendant, Female, an elderly. Dark olive-green high-collared official's tunic. A tiny official on a tall platform telling a family without papers to go away.

starts.name: (Party) The Western Air Temple
starts.info:
PARTY · Book Three · 2-5 players · Aang, Katara, Sokka and Toph · guided
📍 Western Air Temple, The Four Nations. One of the four Air Temples, in the mountains north of the Fire Nation, built under the edge of a cliff with its spires pointing down so that nobody who did not know would see it.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 10-24)

The invasion failed on the day of the eclipse, and Team Avatar has fled to the empty Western Air Temple to hide. The party is with them, the comet is weeks away, and someone has just climbed down the cliff asking to talk.

starts.name: A Prodigy at Court
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · lightning · guided
📍 Royal Plaza, The Four Nations. The long forum in the harbour just below the Fire Nation Capital, where the royal family holds rallies and the army parades, and the capital's main line of defence: battlements, catapults and a gate between cliffs that an invader cannot go around without miles of detour.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 12-30)

The capital is at its proudest: parades, academies and Agni Kai settled at dawn. Lightning is the art of the royal family and a few masters, and somebody has seen you do it.

starts.name: Awakening in the Ice
starts.info:
AVATAR · Book One · the Avatar's own story · guided
📍 Wolf Cove, The Four Nations. The Southern Water Tribe's village on the shore of the South Pole continent: a handful of igloos and tents behind a low snow wall, with a watchtower that leans.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 1-12)

You went into the ice a hundred years ago and came out of it this morning. The world you remember is gone, your people are a story, and two children of the Southern Water Tribe have just pulled you out of a cracked berg.
🎭 Katara, Female, the last waterbender of the Southern Water Tribe. Blue tunic with white trim and dark blue leggings. A girl splashing water at her brother in a canoe, and the water doing what she wants.
🎭 Sokka, Male, Fifteen, the oldest boy left in the Southern Water Tribe village and its self-appointed. Plain blue tunic with white sleeves. A boy with a boomerang guarding a snow wall against an enemy that has not come in years.

starts.name: Ba Sing Se Free
starts.info:
ERA · After the comet · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Lower Ring, The Four Nations. The outermost residential ring of Ba Sing Se, home to the city's poor and most of its people: industries, food, cloth, medicine, slums, and the refugees the ferry brings every day.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 6-30)

Ba Sing Se has its Earth King back, the Dai Li are scattered, and the walls between the rings are suddenly the only thing anyone wants to talk about. The Lower Ring is where the talk is loudest.
🎭 Animal Control Officer, Male, an officer of Ba Sing Se who catches stray animals in the Lower Ring and locks them up. Olive green and cream long tunic with a yellow sash. An officer on a slum street netting a stray and smiling about the price it will fetch.
🎭 Jin, Female, a refugee girl of sixteen living in the Lower Ring of Ba Sing Se. Simple pale green dress. A delivery girl in the Lower Ring grinning at a sullen young man and asking his name.
🎭 Tycho, Male, a mugger of the Lower Ring who always dreamed of going to the university. Ragged brown tunic. A nervous young man stepping out of an alley with a knife and an apology.

starts.name: Contract on the Avatar
starts.info:
ERA · Book Three · combustion · guided
📍 Ash Market, The Four Nations. The capital's common market on the lower crater floor, under red awnings grey with ash: fire flakes, komodo sausage, cloth, charms, the war news on a board, and the Domestic Forces strolling through it.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 12-24)

The war news is posted on a board in the capital's ash market, and today it says the Avatar may be alive. Somebody has hired an assassin with a third eye on his forehead, and the assassin is reading the board too.
🎭 Combustion Man, Male, a huge, silent firebending assassin with a metal arm and leg and an eye tattooed. Sleeveless dark grey armour. A giant at the bounty board with a metal arm, reading the price on a face.

starts.name: Ember Island Summer
starts.info:
ERA · Book Three · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Ember Island, The Four Nations. The Fire Nation's resort island in the outer islands to the north: black-sand beaches, palm trees, luxurious vacation homes for the wealthy and the powerful, kuai ball on the sand and the Ember Island Players at the theater.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 6-24)

The Fire Nation's resort island is full of rich young people, kuai ball and bonfires, and the princess and her friends have come for the summer. Everyone is trying very hard to have fun.
🎭 Chan, Male, the son of an admiral and a popular teenager on Ember Island. A rich boy on Ember Island inviting strangers to a party at his father's house.
🎭 Ruon-Jian, Male, Chan's childhood best friend and a fixture of Ember Island's elite. Loose dark red and gold open robe. A bored boy at a beach party flipping his hair instead of answering.

starts.name: Fever at Taku
starts.info:
HOOK · Book One · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Taku, The Four Nations. A largely abandoned city on the shore of the north-western Earth Kingdom, its walls fallen and its streets empty since the war's early years.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-15)

Someone the party loves is burning with fever, and the only cure anyone knows of is a pair of frozen frogs and the advice of an old herbalist who lives with her cat in the ruins of Taku.
🎭 The Herbalist, Female, an old woman of eighty who lives alone with her cat. Green robe with a dark green collar. An old woman in a ruined town offering a cure and a long story about her cat.

starts.name: Fire Fountain City
starts.info:
ERA · Book Three · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Fire Fountain City, The Four Nations. A large industrial city on the second island of the Fire Nation, named for the great statue of Fire Lord Ozai at its centre with flame pouring from its hands.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 6-20)

Fire Fountain City is loud, proud and loyal, and a statue of the Fire Lord pours fire from its hands over the square. Somewhere in the crowd, a con is being run, and somewhere else a hunter with a metal arm is listening.
🎭 Mayor of Fire Fountain City, Male, the town authority of Fire Fountain City. Small dark eyes, black and red official's robes with a high collar. A mayor on the steps below the fire-breathing statue, reading a proclamation.

starts.name: Fog over Chameleon Bay
starts.info:
ERA · Book Two · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Chameleon Bay Camp, The Four Nations. The camp of the Southern Water Tribe's warriors on Chameleon Bay, tents under the trees, cutters pulled up, Hakoda's map table and Bato's cook fire.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 9-21)

The Southern Water Tribe's warriors are camped on Chameleon Bay, two years from home, waiting for orders and for news. Hakoda has a plan for the eclipse and not enough people to carry it out.

starts.name: General Fong's Fortress
starts.info:
ERA · Book Two · 1-5 players · guided
📍 General Fong's fortress, The Four Nations. A secluded Earth Kingdom military base in the mountains of the west coast, one of the last strongholds of the Earth Kingdom in the region, with barracks, an infirmary, a temple and guest quarters.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 6-18)

General Fong has seen what the Avatar State can do, and he wants it for the war. He has invited the Avatar to his fortress, he has a plan to force it, and he has not asked anyone else what they think.
🎭 General Fong, Male, a powerful earthbender and high-ranking general of the Earth Kingdom's army. Green and tan general's armour with shoulder guards and a dark green cape. A general welcoming the Avatar to his fortress with a parade.
🎭 Aang, Male, a boy of twelve frozen in a sphere of ice somewhere in the southern sea. Yellow and orange monk robes with a high collar. A glowing sphere in the ice floe, and a boy inside it who might still be alive.
🎭 Appa, Male, a ten-ton sky bison with six legs. Small brown eyes. A huge white beast asleep in the ice beside the glowing sphere.
🎭 Katara, Female, the last waterbender of the Southern Water Tribe. Blue tunic with white trim and dark blue leggings. A girl splashing water at her brother in a canoe, and the water doing what she wants.
🎭 Sokka, Male, Fifteen, the oldest boy left in the Southern Water Tribe village and its self-appointed. Plain blue tunic with white sleeves. A boy with a boomerang guarding a snow wall against an enemy that has not come in years.
🎭 Toph, Female, Twelve, blind since birth. Pale unfocused seafoam green eyes, pale cream sleeveless overshirt over a green tunic. A blind girl in the Earth Rumble ring throwing grown men out of it.

starts.name: Ice and Custom
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Canal Market, The Four Nations. The market along the main canal of Agna Qel'a, boats and stalls selling furs, fish, carvings and the goods of a city that trades with nobody but itself.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 12-24)

The Northern Water Tribe's city sits behind walls of ice, and its customs are older than the war. Girls learn healing, boys learn to fight, and nobody questions it out loud.

starts.name: Kyoshi Island Watch
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Suki's village, The Four Nations. A small farming village on Kyoshi Island, the most isolationist on the island and the home of Suki and the Kyoshi Warriors, who drill in the dojo and guard the shore.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-12)

Kyoshi Island has kept the war away for a century by keeping strangers out. The warriors drill in their painted faces, and the village ties up anyone who lands without a reason.
🎭 Suki, Female, the leader of the Kyoshi Warriors of Kyoshi Island. Pale olive green kimono armour with a dark brown chest plate. A girl in white face paint teaching a cocky boy a lesson in her dojo.

starts.name: Lower Ring Arrivals
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Lower Ring, The Four Nations. The outermost residential ring of Ba Sing Se, home to the city's poor and most of its people: industries, food, cloth, medicine, slums, and the refugees the ferry brings every day.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 6-30)

Inside the walls of Ba Sing Se there is no war, the officials say, and nobody asks twice. The Lower Ring is full of people who came from outside and are learning not to talk about it.
🎭 The Corncob Man, Male, a resident of Ba Sing Se who rides the monorail from place to place with a vacant. Baggy green robe with a wide brown collar. A man on the monorail with a corncob in his mouth, staring past everyone.
🎭 The Ticket Woman, Female, a strict worker at the Ba Sing Se monorail who stamps tickets for everyone boarding. Heavy-lidded sly eyes, loose dark olive-green robe with a crossed collar and wide sleeves. A ticket checker at the monorail gate stamping tickets and refusing a refugee.

starts.name: Piandao's Gate
starts.info:
ERA · Book Three · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Shu Jing, The Four Nations. A small, peaceful town on a cliff of waterfalls on one of the eastern islands, one of the many settlements tucked away in the Fire Islands and far from the war.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 6-18)

Above the waterfall town of Shu Jing stands the castle of Piandao, the greatest swordmaster in the Fire Nation. He takes few students, and he decides who by how they knock.

starts.name: Rebuilding the South
starts.info:
ERA · After the comet · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Old Southern Harbour, The Four Nations. The ruin of the Southern Water Tribe's old harbour city, left when the raids took the benders who built it, broken walls of stone and ice that the village lives beside and does not use.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Quiet ground; trouble here is social before it is lethal. (Recommended Level 1-9)

The war is over, and the Southern Water Tribe's men are coming home to the ruin of the harbour city the raids broke. The village has to become something bigger, and Kanna has opinions about how.

starts.name: Refugee Road
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · 1-5 players · guided
📍 River village, The Four Nations. A medium-sized Earth Kingdom town between the forks of a large river on the Mo Ce coast, a regional trading hub where merchants sell whatever the river brings.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 3-18)

The war has pushed another village off its land, and the road to the river ferries is full of people carrying everything they own. You are on it, or you are one of the few people on it with a reason to be going the other way.
🎭 River Village Ferry Master, Male, the ferry master of the river village where the roads of the Mo Ce coast meet the river. A ferry master at the landing waving a family of refugees aboard and telling them to pay him later.

starts.name: Runaway from Gaoling
starts.info:
ERA · Book Two · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Gaoling, The Four Nations. A large, old town in the mountains of the southern Earth Kingdom, rich at the top and poor at the bottom, with the Beifong Estate above it and Earth Rumble, the earthbending tournament, in its arena.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 3-15)

The Beifongs' blind daughter has run away with the Avatar's friends, and her father is paying to have her brought home. Xin Fu and Master Yu have taken the job, and they need more hands.
🎭 Xin Fu, Male, the promoter and announcer of the Earth Rumble. Dark brown and olive sleeveless tunic. A promoter in an arena shouting the champion's name to a roaring crowd.

starts.name: Sandbenders of Si Wong
starts.info:
ERA · Book Two · sandbending · guided
📍 Sandbender Camp, The Four Nations. A camp of the Si Wong tribes in a dune hollow, tents and sand-sailers, a chief and his sons, the rules of the desert and no others.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 12-24)

The sandbenders of the Si Wong rule the desert by its own law: water is given, and theft is answered. Someone has stolen a sky bison, someone has stolen a sand-sailer, and the tribes are blaming each other.
🎭 Sha-Mo, Male, a sandbender of importance in his tribe. Layered tan desert robe and wrap. A sandbender elder in a hollow among the dunes offering water to strangers before asking their names.
🎭 Ghashiun, Male, the teenage son of the sandbender Sha-Mo. Layered tan desert wrappings and sash. A sandbender boy on a sand-sailer circling travellers and grinning behind his face wrap.

starts.name: School Days
starts.info:
ERA · Book Three · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Fire Nation school, The Four Nations. A centre of learning in the eastern Fire Nation where the children recite the oath, learn the official history of the war and are forbidden to dance.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 6-14)

There is a new student at the school in the eastern Fire Nation, from the colonies, they say. The headmaster does not like new students, and he does not like dancing.
🎭 Aang, Male, a boy of twelve frozen in a sphere of ice somewhere in the southern sea. Yellow and orange monk robes with a high collar. A glowing sphere in the ice floe, and a boy inside it who might still be alive.
🎭 Katara, Female, the last waterbender of the Southern Water Tribe. Blue tunic with white trim and dark blue leggings. A girl splashing water at her brother in a canoe, and the water doing what she wants.
🎭 Sokka, Male, Fifteen, the oldest boy left in the Southern Water Tribe village and its self-appointed. Plain blue tunic with white sleeves. A boy with a boomerang guarding a snow wall against an enemy that has not come in years.
🎭 Toph, Female, Twelve, blind since birth. Pale unfocused seafoam green eyes, pale cream sleeveless overshirt over a green tunic. A blind girl in the Earth Rumble ring throwing grown men out of it.
🎭 Hide, Male, a student and the star pupil of the Fire Nation school. Dark red and black school uniform with a high gold-trimmed collar. A bully cornering a smaller boy behind the school.
🎭 The Headmaster, Male, the headmaster of a Fire Nation school on an island town. Dark red and black robe with gold trim. A headmaster shouting at a student for not bowing correctly.

starts.name: Snow Wall Watch
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Wolf Cove, The Four Nations. The Southern Water Tribe's village on the shore of the South Pole continent: a handful of igloos and tents behind a low snow wall, with a watchtower that leans.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 1-12)

Every man of fighting age has gone to the war, and the Southern Water Tribe's last village is women, children and elders behind a wall of packed snow. Sokka has made himself its warrior, and he needs help.
🎭 Katara, Female, the last waterbender of the Southern Water Tribe. Blue tunic with white trim and dark blue leggings. A girl splashing water at her brother in a canoe, and the water doing what she wants.
🎭 Sokka, Male, Fifteen, the oldest boy left in the Southern Water Tribe village and its self-appointed. Plain blue tunic with white sleeves. A boy with a boomerang guarding a snow wall against an enemy that has not come in years.
🎭 Kanna, Female, the oldest resident of the Southern Water Tribe's village at Wolf Cove. Lavender and purple parka with thick white fur hood trim. An old woman at the snow wall watching the sea for a sail she has waited years to see.
🎭 Water Tribe Girl, Female, one of the children of Wolf Cove. A little girl tugging a stranger's sleeve to ask where they came from.

starts.name: Tea at Pao's
starts.info:
ERA · Book Two · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Lower Ring, The Four Nations. The outermost residential ring of Ba Sing Se, home to the city's poor and most of its people: industries, food, cloth, medicine, slums, and the refugees the ferry brings every day.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 6-30)

The Pao Family Tea House in the Lower Ring has a new old man making the tea, and suddenly it is the best tea in the city. His sullen nephew serves it. Neither of them is who they say.
🎭 Lower Ring Guard, Male, a guard of the Lower Ring who drinks his tea at Pao's after his shift. Short black hair, olive green uniform tunic with a dark belt. An off-duty guard at Pao's tea house watching a scene with interest and doing nothing.
🎭 Pao, Male, the owner of the Pao Family Tea House in the Lower Ring of Ba Sing Se. Black vest over a long-sleeved pale green shirt. A tea house owner bowing to a customer and apologising for the tea before they have tasted it.

starts.name: The Avatar After the War
starts.info:
AVATAR · After the comet · the Avatar's own story · guided
📍 Jasmine Dragon, The Four Nations. A traditional tea shop in the Upper Ring, a failing business until an old refugee tea-maker took it over and made it the best in the city, named for drama, poetry and a nice ring.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 6-24)

The Avatar faced the Fire Lord under the comet and won, and the war that lasted a hundred years is over. Now the Avatar has to learn what an Avatar does in peace, which no one alive remembers.
🎭 Iroh, Male, a retired general of the Fire Nation and once its crown prince. Dark red armoured robe over a gold collar. An old man at a Fire Navy pier haggling for a rare white jade bush.
🎭 Appa, Male, a ten-ton sky bison with six legs. Small brown eyes. A huge white beast asleep in the ice beside the glowing sphere.
🎭 Katara, Female, the last waterbender of the Southern Water Tribe. Blue tunic with white trim and dark blue leggings. A girl splashing water at her brother in a canoe, and the water doing what she wants.
🎭 Sokka, Male, Fifteen, the oldest boy left in the Southern Water Tribe village and its self-appointed. Plain blue tunic with white sleeves. A boy with a boomerang guarding a snow wall against an enemy that has not come in years.
🎭 Suki, Female, the leader of the Kyoshi Warriors of Kyoshi Island. Pale olive green kimono armour with a dark brown chest plate. A girl in white face paint teaching a cocky boy a lesson in her dojo.
🎭 Toph, Female, Twelve, blind since birth. Pale unfocused seafoam green eyes, pale cream sleeveless overshirt over a green tunic. A blind girl in the Earth Rumble ring throwing grown men out of it.

starts.name: The Avatar in Disguise
starts.info:
AVATAR · Book Three · the Avatar's own story · guided
📍 Fire Nation bazaar, The Four Nations. A large open-air market in the eastern Fire Nation selling top-quality Fire Nation goods: top-knot rings, headgear, eye patches, jewellery, food, and clothes that let a stranger pass for a local.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 6-18)

Everyone believes the Avatar died in Ba Sing Se. The Avatar did not, and is now in the Fire Nation itself, buying local clothes and learning to pass for a local before the comet comes.

starts.name: The Blind Bandit's Ring
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · metalbending · guided
📍 Gaoling, The Four Nations. A large, old town in the mountains of the southern Earth Kingdom, rich at the top and poor at the bottom, with the Beifong Estate above it and Earth Rumble, the earthbending tournament, in its arena.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 3-15)

Earth Rumble draws crowds to Gaoling every week, and there are rumours of a champion who has never lost. You came to fight, to bet or to find out what a bender can do with metal when nobody has told them it is impossible.
🎭 The Big Bad Hippo, Male, an enormous earthbending wrestler of the Earth Rumble who fights by sheer mass. A huge wrestler biting a rock in half to roars from the crowd.
🎭 The Boulder, Male, a professional earthbending wrestler of the Earth Rumble. A huge wrestler in the ring telling the crowd that the Boulder is ready to rumble.
🎭 Xin Fu, Male, the promoter and announcer of the Earth Rumble. Dark brown and olive sleeveless tunic. A promoter in an arena shouting the champion's name to a roaring crowd.
🎭 Fire Nation Man, Male, an Earth Rumble fighter who plays the villain under the stage name Fire Nation Man. A wrestler in a red costume shaking his fist at a booing crowd.
🎭 Headhunter, Male, an Earth Rumble competitor who wears colourful face paint and fights with wild. Spiky brown hair, white and yellow face paint like a mask with black eye markings. A face-painted wrestler roaring at the crowd before charging.
🎭 The Gecko, Male, an Earth Rumble contestant in a bright green mask who fights on all fours. Full bright green wrestling mask with dark eye patches and red lips covering his head. A masked wrestler clinging to the arena wall and hissing at the crowd.

starts.name: The Blue Spirit's Night
starts.info:
ERA · Book One · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Pohuai Stronghold, The Four Nations. A Fire Nation fortress in the western Earth Kingdom near the ruins of Taku, three walls deep, commanded by Shinu, its colonel, and home to the Yuyan Archers, who can pin a fly to a tree at a hundred paces.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 9-18)

Admiral Zhao has the Avatar locked in the Pohuai Stronghold, and the whole fortress is waiting for the Fire Lord's orders. Tonight a masked thief with two swords is going over the walls, and so are you.
🎭 Colonel Shinu, Male, the commander of the Pohuai Stronghold and the director of the Yuyan Archers. Dark red armour with black plates and shoulder guards. A colonel on the fortress wall watching his archers hit targets at a hundred paces.

starts.name: The Boiling Rock
starts.info:
ERA · Book Three · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Boiling Rock, The Four Nations. The Fire Nation's maximum-security prison, on a volcanic island in the middle of a boiling lake inside a crater, reached only by a gondola over the steam.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 12-24)

Nobody has ever escaped the Boiling Rock, a prison on an island in a boiling lake inside a volcano. The party is inside: as prisoners, as guards, or as people who came to get someone out.
🎭 The Warden of the Boiling Rock, Male, the chief authority of the Boiling Rock. Black and dark red uniform with a high collar. A warden in a steaming prison yard telling a new inmate that no one has ever escaped.
🎭 Chit Sang, Male, an inmate of the Boiling Rock who swears he was falsely accused and defies the guards. Short slicked-back black hair, sleeveless grey prisoner tunic. A prisoner in the yard picking a fight with a guard and grinning about it.
🎭 Suki, Female, the leader of the Kyoshi Warriors of Kyoshi Island. Pale olive green kimono armour with a dark brown chest plate. A girl in white face paint teaching a cocky boy a lesson in her dojo.

starts.name: The Caravan at Misty Palms
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Misty Palms Oasis, The Four Nations. A town on the south-western edge of the Si Wong Desert, grown from a seedy cantina around a spring of ice that is melting.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 9-27)

Misty Palms Oasis is a town that should not exist: a spring in the desert, a cantina, and caravans that only cross the Si Wong when the sandbenders allow it. The spring is drying.

starts.name: The Colonies Question
starts.info:
ERA · After the comet · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Fire Nation colonial village, The Four Nations. A small Fire Nation colonial village in the north-western Earth Kingdom, a cultural centre of the colonies famous for its Fire Days Festival of fireworks, masks and firebending shows.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-15)

The war is over, and the colonies are the question nobody can answer. Families who have lived here for three generations call it home; the Earth King calls it his.
🎭 Festival Guard Captain, Male, the Fire Army captain in charge of security at the Fire Days Festival in the colonial. Dark red and black soldier's uniform. A guard captain at the festival gate waving masked crowds through.

starts.name: The Colony Festival
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Fire Nation colonial village, The Four Nations. A small Fire Nation colonial village in the north-western Earth Kingdom, a cultural centre of the colonies famous for its Fire Days Festival of fireworks, masks and firebending shows.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-15)

The colony's fire festival fills the street with masks, fireworks and firebending shows. Half the crowd were born here and call themselves Fire Nation; the other half are not so sure.
🎭 Ty Lee, Female, a cheerful acrobat of the Fire Nation circus. An acrobat in pink flipping off a tightrope to land beside you and tell you your aura is lovely.
🎭 Malu, Male, a travelling firebending magician who tours the colonies and the Fire Nation. Red and white showman's outfit with gold cuffs and a high red collar. A magician at the festival calling a masked stranger up to help with a trick.
🎭 Shuzumu, Male, the ringleader and manager of a Fire Nation circus touring the colonies. Red robe over a yellow collar. A ringleader under a striped tent, promising the crowd the greatest show in the colonies.

starts.name: The Dam at Gaipan
starts.info:
ERA · Book One · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Gaipan, The Four Nations. A small village in the western Earth Kingdom under Fire Nation occupation, in a river valley below a dam, where the soldiers take what they want and the villagers keep their heads down.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-15)

Jet's Freedom Fighters have a plan to drive the Fire Nation out of Gaipan for good. It involves the dam above the village, a great deal of blasting jelly, and the village itself.

starts.name: The Day of Black Sun
starts.info:
ERA · Book Three · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Royal Plaza, The Four Nations. The long forum in the harbour just below the Fire Nation Capital, where the royal family holds rallies and the army parades, and the capital's main line of defence: battlements, catapults and a gate between cliffs that an invader cannot go around without miles of detour.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 12-30)

The invasion is here. On the day of the solar eclipse the Earth Kingdom, the Water Tribes and every friend the Avatar has made are landing at the Fire Nation Capital, because for eight minutes no firebender can bend.

starts.name: The Deserter's Trail
starts.info:
HOOK · Book One · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Harbor town, The Four Nations. A small coastal settlement in the south-western Earth Kingdom that stayed free of Fire Nation control through the war, a fishing and trading town with a market and a harbour.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-12)

Somewhere in the woods past the free harbour town lives a Fire Navy admiral who walked away from the war, and the Fire Navy wants him back. Some people go looking for him to learn; others go to collect a bounty.

starts.name: The Drill
starts.info:
ERA · Book Two · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Outer Wall, The Four Nations. The outer wall of Ba Sing Se, the greatest wall in the world, raised and held by earthbenders, with the Agrarian Zone's farms behind it and the plain before it.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 9-30)

The Outer Wall of Ba Sing Se has never fallen. Now a Fire Nation drill the size of a town is boring toward it across the plain, and the Terra Team does not know how to stop it.
🎭 General Sung, Male, a general of the Earth Kingdom's army and a member of the Council of Five. Droopy half-closed dark eyes, dark green cloak over gold armour plates. A general on the Outer Wall assuring visitors that nothing has ever broken through.
🎭 Terra Team Captain, Male, the captain of the Terra Team. A coloured round helmet and green armour. A captain on the wall drilling his platoon in formation as the sun rises.

starts.name: The Fleet Off Kyoshi
starts.info:
ERA · Book One · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Kyoshi Landing, The Four Nations. The island's fishing port below Kyoshi's statue, where the elephant koi are landed and the mainland traders buy them.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-12)

A Fire Navy ship has dropped anchor off Kyoshi Island, and its banished prince has come ashore looking for the Avatar. The warriors are ready, the village is frightened, and the island's peace ends tonight.

starts.name: The Foggy Swamp
starts.info:
ERA · Book Two · plantbending · guided
📍 Foggy Swamp Tribe, The Four Nations. The village of the Foggy Swamp Tribe, one of the three Water Tribes, descended from southerners who settled the swamp long ago and bend the water in vines and fog their own way.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 6-18)

The great swamp in the south of the Earth Kingdom takes travellers in and shows them visions of the dead. Its tribe bends water through vines and roots, and says the whole swamp is one tree.
🎭 Due, Male, a waterbender of the Foggy Swamp Tribe who lives on the stilt village with Tho and Huu. Vine wraps on the forearms. A smiling swamp man on his porch who waves and says nothing.
🎭 Tho, Male, a waterbender of the Foggy Swamp Tribe and a close friend of Huu and Due. Short messy brown hair. A swamp bender on a raft, offering a stranger a bug to eat.

starts.name: The Forest Above Gaipan
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Gaipan, The Four Nations. A small village in the western Earth Kingdom under Fire Nation occupation, in a river valley below a dam, where the soldiers take what they want and the villagers keep their heads down.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-15)

Gaipan is occupied: soldiers in the garrison house, villagers keeping their heads down, and in the forest above the dam a band of orphans who call themselves Freedom Fighters.

starts.name: The Fortuneteller's Mountain
starts.info:
ERA · Book One · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Makapu Village, The Four Nations. A small farming village on the slopes of Mt.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-12)

Makapu Village lives by Aunt Wu's fortunes, and Aunt Wu says the volcano will not erupt this year. The clouds say otherwise, and so does the smoke from the crater.
🎭 Aunt Wu, Female, the fortuneteller of Makapu Village. Mustard yellow robe with a brown shawl. A fortuneteller at her door inviting a traveller in for a free reading.
🎭 Meng, Female, Aunt Wu's young assistant. Pink wrap dress with a purple collar band. A girl carrying snacks into a waiting room and staring at a visitor a little too long.
🎭 Poi, Male, one of identical twin brothers of Makapu Village who dress as mirror images. Olive-green robe with a cream spiral shoulder pad. A young man bending a rock into the air to impress a girl, while his identical twin rolls his eyes.
🎭 The Calm Man, Male, an old man of Makapu Village who has complete faith in Aunt Wu's predictions. Dark blue robe over a white collar. An old man standing perfectly still while a bear sniffs him, smiling.

starts.name: The Full Moon Inn
starts.info:
ERA · Book Three · bloodbending · guided
📍 Hama's village, The Four Nations. A small town on one of the central islands, where people have been disappearing on full-moon nights for years and the townsfolk blame a moon monster.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 6-18)

People in this island town vanish on the nights of the full moon. The innkeeper is a kind old woman from far to the south who makes wonderful pie, and tonight the moon is full.
🎭 Hama, Female, a kindly old innkeeper of a small Fire Nation village. Dark shadows around her eyes, ragged dark red robe. A kind old innkeeper at her door, inviting young travellers in out of the cold.

starts.name: The Gondola Runs Empty
starts.info:
ERA · After the comet · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Boiling Rock, The Four Nations. The Fire Nation's maximum-security prison, on a volcanic island in the middle of a boiling lake inside a crater, reached only by a gondola over the steam.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 12-24)

The new Fire Lord has ordered the Boiling Rock's prisoners released, and the gondola over the boiling lake is carrying them out one car at a time. Not all of them should be free, and not all of the guards agree.

starts.name: The Hidden Avatar
starts.info:
AVATAR · Before the iceberg · the Avatar's own story · guided
📍 Kolau Mountain Range, The Four Nations. The great chain of mountains of the south-western Earth Kingdom, the birthplace of earthbending, holding Omashu on one peak and the Cave of Two Lovers under another.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 6-24)

No one has seen the Avatar in a hundred years, because you have been hidden. Someone found you as a child, knew what you were and took you into the mountains. Now the Fire Nation is searching the passes, and the hiding is over.

starts.name: The Library in the Sand
starts.info:
ERA · Book Two · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Misty Palms Oasis, The Four Nations. A town on the south-western edge of the Si Wong Desert, grown from a seedy cantina around a spring of ice that is melting.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 9-27)

A professor of Ba Sing Se University is in the oasis cantina with a map to a library that no one has seen in a thousand years: the spirit Wan Shi Tong's, sunk somewhere under the Si Wong.
🎭 Cantina Keeper, Female, the keeper of the cantina at Misty Palms Oasis. A stained apron over desert robes. A cantina keeper pouring cactus juice and warning a newcomer not to drink too much of it.
🎭 Fung, Male, a crafty old man of Misty Palms Oasis who plays Pai Sho in the cantina for money. Plain brown robe with an olive collar. An old man in the oasis cantina inviting a stranger to a game of Pai Sho, and watching which tile they play.

starts.name: The Mail Chutes of Omashu
starts.info:
HOOK · Before the iceberg · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Omashu, The Four Nations. The second city of the Earth Kingdom, built up a peak of the Kolau Mountain Range in stepped terraces, with the delivery system's chutes running down it on earthbending and gravity.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 6-24)

Omashu has never fallen. King Bumi rules it from the top of the mountain, its chutes carry everything up and down the terraces, and its gate has turned back every army.

starts.name: The New Fire Lord
starts.info:
ERA · After the comet · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Fire Nation Capital, The Four Nations. The seat of the Fire Nation, built inside the crater of a dead volcano on Capital Island.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 12-30)

Zuko has been crowned Fire Lord, his father is in prison and his sister is in an asylum. Half the court thinks he is a traitor, and the other half is waiting to see whether he is weak.
🎭 Palace Gate Captain, Male, the captain of the Domestic Forces guard at the capital's palace gate. Red and black guard armour with a captain's helmet. A gate captain stopping a cart at the palace road and reading its papers aloud.
🎭 Azula's Servant, Female, one of the many servants of the Fire Nation's royal family. Plain dark red servant's robe. A palace servant at the gate hurrying past with a tray and her eyes on the ground.

starts.name: The Prison Rig
starts.info:
ERA · Book One · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Seaport village, The Four Nations. A small coastal settlement on the Mo Ce Sea, an important port captured by the Fire Nation, where coal from inland is loaded into warships before they go out to sea.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 3-15)

Earthbenders who fight back are taken to a metal prison rig at sea, where there is no earth to bend. The coaling village across the water watches the ships come and go and does not ask who is on them.

starts.name: The Retired Raider
starts.info:
ERA · Book Three · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Yon Rha's village, The Four Nations. A minor settlement in the hilly, rainy south of the Fire Nation, where a retired Southern Raiders commander lives with his mother and does the shopping.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 6-18)

A man who once led a raid on the Southern Water Tribe lives quietly now in a rainy village in the Fire Nation, buying vegetables for his mother. Someone has come a very long way to find him.
🎭 Yon Rha, Male, a retired officer of the Fire Navy who lives quietly in a small Fire Nation village. Faded dark red robe. An ordinary old man in a village market buying vegetables for his mother.

starts.name: The River Spirit
starts.info:
ERA · Book Three · 1-5 players · guided
📍 Jang Hui, The Four Nations. A small fishing village of houseboats and stilt houses in the middle of the Jang Hui River, joined by bridges and planks, on one of the outer islands.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 6-18)

Jang Hui is a village of houseboats on a river poisoned by the factory upstream. The fish are thin, the children are sick, and at night the Painted Lady comes to help them.
🎭 Dock, Male, the ferryman of Jang Hui. A ferryman at a rotting dock offering to carry you across, then introducing his brother in another hat.

starts.name: The Serpent's Pass
starts.info:
ERA · Book Two · 1-5 players · guided
